events.title: Peter Angelo: Standup Comedy Show
events.description:
Performing Live:

Peter Angelo
With:
Wonder Dave

Picture this: a gay metalhead truck driver walks into a comedy club. It sounds like the setup to a joke, but it actually perfectly describes our headliner -- Peter \"Metal Pete\" Angelo. Peter is a stand-up comedian based in Austin, Texas, who traded a career in truck driving for the stage. For eight years, he toured the country in an 18-wheeler, presumably blasting Death Metal while navigating both America's highways and his own journey of self-discovery. Coming out of the closet is hard enough without having to do it at truck stops from coast to coast. Peter's comedy breaks every stereotype you can think of, proving you can't judge a book by its cover, especially when that cover features leather jackets, muscles, and an inexplicable knowledge of both diesel engines and show tunes.

Wonder Dave is a comedian, writer and performer from Minneapolis, MN, living in California. He hosts and produces Safe Words Showcase - Queer Sex Positive Comedy and SMILF - Straight Men I'd Like to Friend with producer Jonah Price, hosts Hysteria: Open Mic for Women and Queers, hosts and produces Mental Health Comedy Hour with comedian Kristee Ono, and Co-Hosts Ruckus and Rumpus Revival with Jamie DeWolf.

events.title: Mortified
events.description:
MORTIFIED

Mortified is a comic excavation of adolescent writing, art & media. PS: It totally likes you.

Performers TBA...

Hailed as a \"cultural phenomenon\" by Newsweek and celebrated for years by the likes of This American Life, The Today Show, The Onion AV Club, & Entertainment Weekly, Mortified is a comic excavation of teen angst artifacts (journals, poems, letters, lyrics, home movies, schoolwork) as shared by their original authors -- in front of total strangers!

Where else can you hear grown men and women confront their past with firsthand tales of their first kiss, first puff, worst prom, fights with mom, life at bible camp, worst hand job, best mall job, and reasons they deserved to marry Bon Jovi? Submissions come from a wide range of participants, from professional performers to total amateurs . All in the noble pursuit of self-degradation. Share the shame.

events.title: Terpnami 2026
events.description:
The highest-level genetics conversation in the world returns to the Bay Area this December to help growers worldwide garden harder, better, faster, and stronger.

Over 1,000 growers big and small from around the world interact with 30 of the world’s top breeders over two days December 5 and 6 in a private Bay Area venue for TERPNAMI. Guests can RSVP today to get ticketing and event details.

The world’s first only ‘seed rave,’ Terpnami runs 12 to 5 p.m. Saturday and Sunday, December 5 and 6, with live DJs, visuals, local food, drink, and creative art and merch collabs; plus pre and after-parties, dinners and meetups.

“Terpnami is the most important seed show in the world,” said California breeder Purple Caper.

Why Terpnami 2026?

California remains the global cannabis epicenter for genetic innovation. Virtually every hot strain in the $60 billion U.S. market, and the global cannabis market beyond, traces its roots to genetics bred or popularized in California. Lemon Cherry Gelato, Z, GSC, OG Kush, and GDP are just few California creations.

Terpnami keeps the Bay Area cannabis genetics beacon lit every December, a time of year when the full-sun harvest seeds are shucked and packaged, and folks are flush with cash for Christmas and thinking about what to grow in 2027.

For year three, Terpnami again shifts to a new venue with historic, theatrical features, crucial mass transit access, and more amenities for guests including off-street parking, and a dedicated restaurant. Our...

The MSSF Fungus Fair includes the latest collection of expertly identified fungi collected in various locations in the Bay Area. In the San Francisco Bay Area, when the first rains tease up the chanterelles and porcini, fungus lovers head to the Fungus Fair.

events.title: The Irish Women’s Short Film Festival
events.address: 2700 45th Avenue, SAN FRANCISCO, CA, 94116, United States
events.description:
Join us for an evening of Irish storytelling through film. The Irish Women’s Short Film Festival brings together 11 short films celebrating the voices and visions of women filmmakers in Ireland and across the global Irish diaspora.
TICKETS

From questions of identity and migration to family, grief, faith, resilience, and finding one’s voice, these films explore the many ways women make sense of where they come from—and where they are going. Their stories cross generations and borders, offering moments of honesty, tenderness, strength, and recognition.
Created by co-producers Jeanne McInerney and Orlaith Carr, the festival grew from conversations about womanhood, belonging, inheritance, and the layered experience of being Irish across generations and oceans. Recent Australian screenings in Adelaide, Melbourne, and Sydney sold out, bringing audiences together around stories that resonated across the diaspora.
Come for the films, stay for the company. The evening offers a relaxed, welcoming chance to meet fellow film lovers, creatives, and members of the Irish community—and to share in the conversations these stories inspire.
Bring a friend and join us at the UICC for a memorable night of film and connection.
Space is limited; advance tickets are $15.
notes: Published by United Irish Cultural Center of San Francisco

events.title: Gwar
events.description:
Gwar
Thursday, November 19 | The UC Theatre

The story of GWAR is carved across the history of this hopeless planet, but GWAR themselves are not of this world...Their story begins far past Uranus, in the deepest reaches of space, where the beings known as GWAR were warriors in the Scumdogs of the Universe, an elite fighting force in the army of the Master of All Reality. But GWAR proved too reckless and powerful, and after a series of tragic but hilarious blunders, they were banished to the furthest reaches of the galaxy, with orders to conquer an insignificant backwater prehistoric mudball known as the planet Earth. Once here, GWAR, the original Ancient Aliens, shaped the face of the globe, wiping out the dinosaurs, and mating with apes to create the human race. Having accidentally given rise to all human history, the Master of All Reality froze them in Antarctic ice where they could do no more harm. It was there they were discovered by a shady entrepreneur known as Sleazy P Martini, who sat the band down in front of professional wrestling, late-night horror movies, heavy metal music, and a steady diet of crack cocaine until GWAR became the cultural force they are today!

Forgot how to interact with people in the wild? Accidentally called your boss 'mom' in front of your coworkers and now you don’t know what to do with that? Considered making your dog your emergency contact? Deeply terrified that you’ll never experience true human connection because your primary social outlet is arguing with strangers in subreddits? Well then, talking to actual humans at the Story Exchange may be right for you.

Mission StageWorks invites you to a guided storytelling experience where you can swap true stories and build actual, real-time connections. We provide a supportive space and the story prompts, so there's zero pressure to perform (or be a stand-up comedian). Just an evening of meeting people, discovering you aren't the only one with deeply specific hang ups, and finding community through meaningful conversations.
Meet people – tell stories – find your community – eat snacks

For more information, click here.

events.title: Reimagining the Future with Psilocybin Mushrooms with Paul Stamets
events.description:
CIIS Public Programs presents renowned mycologist and medical researcher Paul Stamets for an illuminating talk on the history of psilocybin mushrooms exploring their past, present, and future uses. In this presentation, Paul takes you on a journey into the psilocybin mycosphere as he chronicles milestones that further substantiate that psilocybin, and more so psilocybin mushrooms, can help us evolve into the best of what we can be.

The collection and cultivation of psilocybin mushrooms, Paul argues, is central to our practices for freedom of consciousness. Paul shares how psilocybin mushrooms might fundamentally change the many challenges we face as a society. He believes we are at an evolutionary crossroads. Could psilocybin mushrooms help propel us as we emerge into a new version of ourselves, Homo sapiens 3.0?

Paul Stamets, D.Sc. (Honoris causa) is a speaker, author, mycologist, medical researcher, and entrepreneur, who is considered an intellectual and industry leader in fungi. He is the founder and owner of Fungi Perfecti, LLC, and Host Defense Mushrooms supplement line. Paul Stamets is the author of eight books. He named numerous new species of psilocybin mushrooms. In 2023, a new psilocybin mushroom species was named after him to honor his lifelong work: "Psilocybe stametsii." events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Computerwife
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Computerwife

New York City-based Addie Warncke began Computerwife in 2018 at the beginning of her college career, using SoundCloud as a diary to chronicle her emotions. When the pandemic hit, Warncke released the five songs she was proudest of as her self-titled debut EP, and the strength of those tracks led to a signing with Danger Collective Records. Now, she’s poised to release her debut self-titled full-length: a raw and intimate portrait of her experiences processing the small but poignant moments that shape a life. Computerwife’s sound is captivating and nuanced, pushing the boundaries between analog and digital. “The main theme that ties this album together is an interest in the deep web and an attempt to combine existing media to make something new,” she explains. With her seamless blend of shoegaze, emo, and lo-fi noise pop, Computerwife speaks directly to the disquiet experienced by every 21st century digital girl with a tenuous grip on life and identity.

Without any prior production knowledge or a band to work with, expanding her songs beyond the writing stage was a challenge Warncke sought to overcome. A Song Exploder episode about Grimes inspired her to download a free trial of Ableton so she could flesh out tracks and learn more about electronic production. On her dorm room bed, she began to record with her dad’s guitar and bass, a Fender deluxe amp, and a focusrite to Ableton. Her first EP and forthcoming debut LP are pulled from thes...

events.title: Larisa Brechun: Somnia
events.description:
Larisa Brechun: Somnia
November 14–December 5

Ryan Graff Contemporary is excited to present Larisa Brechun's debut solo exhibition Somnia.

The subtle qualities of the soul—softness, stillness, fragility, solitude—are often belittled for their “weakness," dismissed as defects of simpering prey in a predatory age, where might and volume rule and humanity fills its hours with chatter and self-exposure. Introspection is the enemy of the social machine, softness a death sentence, silence a grave. And yet, these delicate instincts are essential to the most intimate operation of the soul: the dream.

In Larisa Brechuns’s Somnia, the artist lays bare the quiet privacy of the dreaming mind and the fugitive debris of memory, myth, and imagination as it freely floats in the cocoon of sleep, coalescing into mysterious forms that defy daylight logic. Under her gentle hand, soft animal bodies take shape alongside evaporating cosmic beings and primordial symbols of wilderness, all adrift in the penumbra of the dreaming state, suspended in etheric margins between the deep woodland dark and the flirting light of a winking moon.

Brechun’s darkness has substance, an amplitude of unseen marrow with texture and weight, like a cave or a chrysalis. Lonely figures gently emerge from abyssal thickets, twisting into the light of the omnipresent moon’s awareness as quickly as they recede. They are camouflaged by silence and shadow, hiding by turns in shyness, in stillness, in pain, in contemplation,...

events.title: Trash Prom Walk of Shame: Runway as Performance Art
events.description:
Jordan Joel presents the debut of their newest collection

Trash Prom Walk of Shame

Trash Prom turns shame into spectacle: alchemy, excess and reclamation, built from what the world throws away. The Walk of Shame becomes a walk of pride, a celebration of personal survival in scraps and iridescence.

Here, the discarded is sacred. Trash couture walks alongside upcycled pieces and ready-to-wear, each look in conversation with the others. Together they carry a confession: the things we were told to hide, stitched back together and sent down the runway in full camp glory.

Shame isn’t erased. It’s raw material, and transgression is how it transforms.

Beyond fashion, the night becomes an immersive world of performance art, interactive installations, music and a live atelier.

Join the inaugural Queer Heartstrings, the first iteration of a collective textile creation, and watch transformation happen up close as you become part of the show.

Come as you are, as you were, or as who you’re becoming.
Walk in carrying whatever you’ve been holding, and walk out shining.

Friday, November 20, 2026 · Monument, 140 9th St, San Francisco
Doors: 7:00PM | Show: 8:00PM

events.description:
Layton Giordani continues to reign as a trailblazer and now label boss of MADMINDS in the

house and techno world, solidifying his presence at the forefront of the global scene. A New

York native, Giordani’s journey into electronic music began in his teens, inspired by the

legendary sets of Danny Tenaglia at Pacha NY. This profound experience drove him to pursue a

career behind the decks, eventually securing a pivotal residency at Output NY in Brooklyn.

events.title: Songs, Sermons & Sacred Voyeurism
events.description:
Doors 7:30pm / Show 8pm

Free | RSVP Optional

A live activation in The Chapel of Becoming, organized by Chani Bockwinkel in collaboration with Leila Weefur

Songs, Sermons & Sacred Voyeurism extends the aesthetic and spiritual inquiry of The Chapel of Becoming into the body, the voice, and the act of witness. Part performance, part ritual architecture, the work draws on the long tradition of sacred song as a technology of transformation, and on the peep show as a structure of longing, obscured presence, and controlled revelation.

Performers move through the space using techniques of visual obstruction and partial disclosure, making themselves available to be seen and not, extending the exhibition's meditation on thresholds, devotion, and what it means to become. Simultaneously, visitors are invited into sound experiences where vocal performances unfold in intimate isolation, a format of auditory voyeurism where listening borders on lustful and asks listeners to receive the voice as an act of devotion.

Together these modes, the body in motion and the disembodied voice, produce a devotional space that refuses the separation of the sacred from the sensorial.

Featuring performances by Maxe Crandall, Elya Piazza, Snowflake Arizmendi-Calvert, Alma Carmina Marquexz, Styles Alexander, B Dean, Hands, and Mudd the Two Spirit, with additional performers to be announced.

She writes a weekly column for the Davis Enterprise. This is her third cookbook. She lives with her husband in Davis.

events.title: Larisa Brechun: Somnia
events.description:
Larisa Brechun: Somnia
November 14–December 5

Ryan Graff Contemporary is excited to present Larisa Brechun's debut solo exhibition Somnia.

The subtle qualities of the soul—softness, stillness, fragility, solitude—are often belittled for their “weakness," dismissed as defects of simpering prey in a predatory age, where might and volume rule and humanity fills its hours with chatter and self-exposure. Introspection is the enemy of the social machine, softness a death sentence, silence a grave. And yet, these delicate instincts are essential to the most intimate operation of the soul: the dream.

In Larisa Brechuns’s Somnia, the artist lays bare the quiet privacy of the dreaming mind and the fugitive debris of memory, myth, and imagination as it freely floats in the cocoon of sleep, coalescing into mysterious forms that defy daylight logic. Under her gentle hand, soft animal bodies take shape alongside evaporating cosmic beings and primordial symbols of wilderness, all adrift in the penumbra of the dreaming state, suspended in etheric margins between the deep woodland dark and the flirting light of a winking moon.

Brechun’s darkness has substance, an amplitude of unseen marrow with texture and weight, like a cave or a chrysalis. Lonely figures gently emerge from abyssal thickets, twisting into the light of the omnipresent moon’s awareness as quickly as they recede. They are camouflaged by silence and shadow, hiding by turns in shyness, in stillness, in pain, in contemplation,...

Hired to work on a yacht belonging to the disabled husband of femme fatale Rita Hayworth (Gilda, Separate Tables), Welles plays an innocent man drawn into a dangerous web of intrigue and murder. Decades later, The Lady from Shanghai is considered vintage Welles, his famous hall of mirrors climax hailed as one of the greatest scenes in cinematic history.

events.title: “Castro on Fire”: A Queer Resistance Walking Tour by Unspeakable Vice
events.description:
LOCATION

GLBT Historical Society Museum

4127 18th Street

San Francisco, CA 94114

ADMISSION

$35; Museum admission included in tour

RSVP and reserve tickets here

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

Details

Duration: about 90 minutes, plus the round afterward

Meet: GLBT Historical Society, 4127 18th Street

Ends: the Lookout, 3600 16th St at Market

Terrain: city sidewalks with one moderate hill; the Lookout is upstairs, stairs only

Ages: 21+ (free round, one per guest)

Heavy Rain: tours reschedule; your ticket transfers

Full route teasers, the people you'll meet, and sources: unspeakablevice.tour...

events.title: Visions of Utopia
events.description:
Dive into the collective imagination of what our world could be.

This past year Crystal Vielula - Artist and Owner of Sunshine Art House in Inner Richmond, SF - has been crowdsourcing individuals’ ideas of utopia. She had utopia-themed collage and dance parties so we could take some time imagining a better world together. She took all of those collective imaginings and used them as inspiration for collage dioramas that have dance footage playing inside.
We’re excited to have another opportunity to collectively dream up a better world.

The preview will be held on Wed. Nov. 18th
from 6-8pm and the reception will be on Sat. Nov. 21st from 5-8pm @sunshinearthouse
4338 California St. San Francisco, CA 94118

All of the work was created by hand, analog/cut and paste collage, ceramic sculptures, and giant flower masks worn by dancers and filmed by Myleen Hollero (@hollerotron on Instagram) to create a fun alternative universe where everyone can feel safe, comfortable, and cared for.

Please wear white or light colors so that you can take on the projections in the dance room.

These events are free and open to all.

Thank you to the SF Arts Commission for their support!

events.title: Zhang Yimou’s Raise the Red Lantern (4K Restoration)
events.description:
Co-presented by Bay Area Chinese Culture Salon and Amoment Books.

Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul.

One of international cinema’s greatest stars of the era, Gong Li is “nuanced and understated” (Chicago Reader) as the stifled young woman forced into a repressive world of concubinage. Newly restored, the film stands as one of the defining works of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and international film of the 1990s.

“As visually striking as it is dramatically effective…subtly exploring the politics of power and control” – Janet Maslin, The New York Times

events.title: Lucy Kaplansky
events.description:
She started out singing in Chicago folk music clubs as a teenager. Then, barely out of high school, Lucy Kaplansky took off for New York City. There she found a fertile community of songwriters and performers—Suzanne Vega, Steve Forbert, The Roches, and others. With a beautiful flair for harmony, Lucy was everyone’s favorite singing partner, but most often she found herself singing as a duo with Shawn Colvin. People envisioned big things for them; in fact, The New York Times said it was “easy to predict stardom for her.” But then Lucy dropped it all.

Convinced that her calling was in another direction, Lucy left the musical fast track to pursue a doctorate in clinical psychology. Upon completing her degree, Dr. Kaplansky took a job at a New York hospital working with chronically mentally ill adults, and also started a private practice. Yet she continued to sing. Lucy was often pulled back into the studio by her friends, (who now had contracts with record labels) wanting her to sing on their albums. She harmonized on Colvin’s Grammy-winning "Steady On," and on Nanci Griffith’s "Lone Star State of Mind" and "Little Love Affairs." She also landed soundtrack credits, singing with Suzanne Vega on "Pretty in Pink" and with Griffith on "The Firm," and several commercial credits as well—including “The Heartbeat of America” for Chevrolet.

Then Shawn Colvin—who was itching to produce a record—hooked up with Lucy, her ex-singing partner. They went into the studio, and when Lucy’s solo...

events.title: Welcome to Fear City
events.description:
Welcome to Fear City: NYPD Surveillance Films from The Bureau of Special Services

The NYPD Bureau of Special Services conducted covert surveillance on political and social activists from 1960 to 1980, capturing on film activities of the Civil Rights Movement, Vietnam War protestors, Cold War activists and many more developments of this politically tumultuous period. Now, all 1,450 films have been digitized and made publicly available by the NYC Department of Records.

This special screening features a small selection of these revealing films hosted by the former film archivist from the NYC Department of Records who digitized and preserved these films. Join us for an open discussion and screening of the contents of these silent films where the audience is encouraged to pose their questions to the archivist who worked directly with these historic records.

Brutalismus 3000 are the duo of producer Theo Zeitner and singer Victoria Vassiliki Daldas, two musical visionaries who met on Tinder in 2018 and formed their antagonistic techno band in 2020. With an early hit titled “Satan Was a Babyboomer” and fan-favorite lyrics about “fuckface bouncers,” Brutalismus 3000’s playful attitude and aggressive sound were always too animated for Berlin’s restrictive techno scene. Since the release of their high-voltage 2023 debut, ULTRAKUNST (LIVE FROM EARTH), Brutalismus 3000 have been mainstays of the international festival circuit -- EDC, Primavera Sound, Coachella, Ultra, Lollapalooza, and more -- and now have friends, fans, and collaborators strewn all across the globe.

For their exhilarating sophomore album, Harmony, Brutalismus 3000 aimed to emphasize their cross-continental influences in a way they never have. The record is a genre-mangling triumph that assembles elements of dubstep, trap, punk, nu-metal, and techno into an eclectic romp of wall-to-wall bangers that includes their most evolved and exciting music yet. Never have Brutalismus 3000 sounded this singular, this sophisticated, this outlandishly absorbing. events.title: Pearl
events.description:
The allure of stardom on the big screen proves to be a road to some very dark places for Mia Goth’s titular PEARL in this stylish and gruesome prequel to Ti West’s X. With her husband away at war, Pearl finds herself dreaming of a way to escape from her boring life on the farm. She sees the silver screen as her way to find stardom and the love she so desperately needs, but her overbearing mother and her own dark impulses might hold her back from the fame she craves.

PEARL proves to be a delightfully perverse study on a standout character from writer/director Ti West’s tribute to ‘70s grindhouse, X. Its vibrant, candy-coated veneer plays wonderfully against the depraved desires of the main character bubbling just below the surface. Co-writer/star Mia Goth gives another deliciously unhinged performance as Pearl, a not-quite-innocent farm girl looking for love in all the wrong places. As much a love letter to the Golden Age of Hollywood as it is a demented look at the darkness bubbling just below the surface of rural America, PEARL is colorful, unnerving, and twisted in all the right ways.

Join WNP Film Club on November 22, 2026 for a screening of a San Francisco noir classic, Dark Passage (1947).

In this atmospheric film, Humphrey Bogart stars as Vincent Parry, a San Francisco man who escapes prison after being wrongly convicted of murdering his wife. With the help of a mysterious woman (Lauren Bacall), he attempts to clear his name while evading the police and searching for the real killer. Filmed on location in San Francisco, Dark Passage blends suspense, romance, and shadowy city streets into a classic noir thriller.

WNP Film Club is a 4 Star Theater series brought to you by Western Neighborhoods Project, your friendly community history nonprofit, in partnership with Bay Area Movies (BAM) and Cinema SF Bay. Join us in celebrating movies filmed on location in San Francisco, with a connection to the west side. This screening will feature an introduction by Jason Moore of BAM and WNP’s resident history nerd, who will share some background about the film and featured locations, including “then and now” comparisons with support from Tim Welsh of SF in Film. Optional Extra Credit: stick around after to unpack the movie with us and indulge your inner film nerd.

events.title: Dark Habits
events.description:
Rejected from Cannes for being sacrilegious in its critical depiction of Catholicism’s role in modern Spanish society and marking a major tone shift in Pedro Almodóvar’s filmmaking in the midst of The Movida Madrileña. This piercing psychedelic tale follows cabaret singer Yolanda as she finds refuge in an eccentric convent at risk of financial collapse where the nuns call themselves The Humiliated Redeemers. There, she finds herself among chain-smoking sisters, a pet tiger that can only be soothed by a young Carmen Maura (WOMEN ON THE VERGE OF A NERVOUS BREAKDOWN, VOLVER) playing bongos, and erotic novel smugglers with mustache hairs that blow in the wind. These characters enable each other’s vices and neuroses as they maintain the illusion of seeking salvation under the wing of The Mother Superior, their drug and love addicted leader who uses the mission as a means of luring in needy women. From the deteriorating convent emerges a potent yet playful reminder that we are all sinners that need to be loved.

events.title: Point Blank (1967)
events.description:
British director John Boorman brought a European sensibility to a Los Angeles neo-noir: POINT BLANK is Antonioni plus violence, Francesco Rosi without politics. The title reverberates like a pun-point: blank. Lee Marvin is Walker, left for dead in an Alcatraz heist and now out to find the $93,000 he has coming. No more, no less, unless you count revenge. The trail leads to the City of Angels and the syndicate that runs it out of car lots and Santa Monica penthouses, the kind of places you know exist only with a little larceny. Picking up on the modern surface of his locale, Boorman takes a champagne-blonde color scheme to a hallucinatory degree, blonde on blond, like Angie Dickinson's bouffant and Marvin's silvery pate (here, we have the bad, the brunette, and the bald). Los Angeles is inherently horizontal. The payoff, visually and narratively, occurs in that storm drain affectionately known as the L.A. River, viewed from a bridge over imagined waters. (BAMPFA)

DCP courtesy of Warner Bros.

Now, thirteen years after his landmark debut Anhe Bridge North, arrives his long-awaited second album, Take Another Moment. The Music of Hey Arnold! Live featuring Jim Lang & The PS 118 AllStars celebrates the 30th anniversary of one of television’s most cherished animated series.

Led by award winning composer Jim Lang, best known for his unforgettable theme music, original songs, and score for Hey Arnold!, this one of a kind concert brings the music of the series to life on stage. Blending jazz, hip hop, blues, R&B and funk, Lang created a sound unlike anything else on television, helping give Hey Arnold! its heart, warmth, humor and soul. Performed by Jim Lang and The PS 118 AllStars, the evening features the show’s unforgettable themes, fan favorite songs, and some of the moments that made Hey Arnold! so special. Accompanied by multimedia visuals and stories from behind the music, the performance also includes a special guest appearance by series creator Craig Bartlett.

Whether you grew up with Hey Arnold! or are discovering its music for the first time, this 30th anniversary celebration is a chance to experience one of animation’s most distinctive and enduring scores performed live by the composer who created it.

events.title: The Cook, The Thief, His Wife, & Her Lover
events.description:
Peter Greenaway's 1989 magnum opus THE COOK, THE THIEF, HIS WIFE & HER LOVER is neo-noir for the hungry, devious soul. Released at a time when crime cinema was growing increasingly perverse with the likes of ANGEL HEART (1987), BLUE VELVET (1986), and BODY DOUBLE (1984), Greenaway's film out-shocks the buch by intertwining two of human nature's favorite pastimes: food and sex. Like Marco Ferreri's LA GRAND BOUFFE (1973) and Paul Bartel's EATING RAOUL (1982) before it, food and sex quickly turn into a recipe for something decidedly more sinister and... cannibalistic. Shocking audiences at the time of its release, time has not tamed Greenaway's film at all, and you'll never look at Helen Mirren or Michael Gambon the same way again. (Justin LaLiberty)

events.description:
In a castle in the San Fernando Valley lies the lair of music icon Gary Numan. Outside is an enormous statue of a dragon, inside a St Bernard (almost as large) greets you on arrival. He's a new addition to the family – a rescue pup, and huge. The lord of this manor could be as outwardly intimidating as this entire set-up, but he's a humble presence. Notorious for hits such as 'Are 'Friends' Electric?' and 'Cars', Numan's early career was too often misconstrued, tainted by a sometimes fraught relationship with the media and challenged by the hostility of the music industry at the time, still deeply committed as it was to the guitar, bass, drums approach of old. Numan, however, stuck to his guns, outlasted his naysayers, and became renowned not just as a pioneer but as an institution. Today, with a career that has spanned nearly four decades, his approach to electronic music remains an inspiration to artists across genres and eras, from stadium goliaths such as Depeche Mode, Prince and Nine Inch Nails to alternative heroes such as Beck, Damon Albarn and Marilyn Manson. Even Kanye West owes him a debt and David Bowie once credited him with ‘writing two of the finest songs’ in British music. It's no surprise he recently received the Ivor Novello Award for Inspiration.

Now, Numan is preparing his 22nd studio album titled ' Savage (Songs From A Broken World)'. He's a busy guy. A self-proclaimed “one man band”, Numan has always been something of an outlier living on his own terms....

events.title: The Room Returns
events.description: What happens when great actors collide with the worst script ever written? Tommy Wiseau's original THE ROOM (2003) infamously burned through $6 million and months of shooting with no-name actors. This reimagining flips the myth on its head. Filmed in under 12 hours, on virtually no budget, with Bob Odenkirk (Better Call Saul), Bella Heathcote (THE NEON DEMON), executive producer Mike Flanagan (The Haunting of Hill House), and directed by newcomer Brando Crawford. With no rehearsal and only teleprompters to guide them, the cast embraced the chaos with Shakespearean gravity, transforming cinematic disaster into unpredictable spectacle – all for charity.

events.description:
Jeff Dean is an L.A.-based stand-up comedian, actor, and writer originally from Reno, Nevada. He came up in the San Francisco Bay Area, where his vulnerable, confessional storytelling quickly set him apart and earned him a dedicated following.

His breakout moment came with one of Don't Tell Comedy's most-watched sets, which he parlayed into a distinctive social media presence built around stand-up clips paired with dramatic re-enactments. The result is a devoted cult following — self-dubbed The Dean's List — who have proven they'll show up anywhere he performs.

Jeff has been featured on CBS's Comics Unleashed and at festivals including Netflix Is a Joke Fest, SF SketchFest, and 10,000 Laughs. He's a regular at the Hollywood Improv, Punch Line SF & Sacramento, Cobb's Comedy Club, and The Comedy & Magic Club, and is currently in development at The Comedy Store.

events.title: Dancegiving & Community Ocean Dance
events.description:
An open-air, silent-disco dance experience by the ocean, where music, movement, and community meet to experience life. Let's celebrate!

Join us for Ocean Dance: a unique gathering of movement, music, and magic on the sand.
This is a sacred celebration by the Pacific, a space where community, creativity, and presence meet through dance and breath, guided by the ocean’s rhythm.

From 10:30 AM to 12:00 PM, we come together at Ocean Beach for a silent disco movement journey, led by music from local DJs and curated by Lyrical Poet and movement guide Magalí Clazón. As the sun sets and the full moon rises, we dance to release, reconnect, and remember the simple joy of being alive.

This experience is a moving meditation, no choreography, no expectations, just the invitation to listen to your body, connect to your spirit, and move freely.

This is for you if you’re longing to…
• Dance freely in a safe and supportive space
• Let go of stress and reconnect with your body
• Feel held by community and nature
• Celebrate the full moon in ritual and joy
• Align with the earth’s cycles and your inner rhythm
• Be inspired by live music and poetry under the open sky

Ocean Dance is not a performance, it’s a practice.
It’s a sanctuary for expression, presence, healing, and celebration. Whether you’re new to dance or returning to your body after a long time, you are welcome, just as you are.

events.description: This documentary, made over a period of eight years, tells the remarkable story of an extremely influential rocknroll band. Starting from their mid-60s garage band roots (sounding amazingly like the Sonics), the Motor City 5 deveoped into an icon for a brand of loud, crushing music reflecting their industrial roots. Even if you dont care for their music (and youre bound to like even a few of their songs), their story is fascinating. It combines 60s protest, youthful braggadocio, and a style of music that would help carry one to the likes of Iggy and the Stooges (not to mention certain aspects of punk rock). This film is clearly a labor of love, combining extraordinarily rare live shows, still shots, a nearly-continuous backdrop of MC5 tunes, penetrating interviews with the remaining members and their spouses, and even FBI surveillance shots. Its the ultimate testimonial to a band that only gains in stature as time goes on.

After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.

events.title: The Music of Hey Arnold! Live Ft. Jim Lang and the PS 118 AllStars
events.address: 417 Alvarado Street, Monterey, CA, Monterey, CA, 93940
events.description:
The Music of Hey Arnold! Live featuring Jim Lang & The PS 118 AllStars celebrates the 30th anniversary of one of television's most cherished animated series.

Led by award winning composer Jim Lang, best known for his unforgettable theme music, original songs, and score for Hey Arnold!, this one of a kind concert brings the music of the series to life on stage. Blending jazz, hip hop, blues, R&B and funk, Lang created a sound unlike anything else on television, helping give Hey Arnold! its heart, warmth, humor and soul. Thirty years later, the music continues to connect with fans of all ages and inspire musicians around the world.

Performed by Jim Lang and The PS 118 AllStars, the evening features the show's unforgettable themes, fan favorite songs, and some of the moments that made Hey Arnold! so special. Accompanied by multimedia visuals and stories from behind the music, the performance also includes a special guest appearance by series creator Craig Bartlett.

Whether you grew up with Hey Arnold! or are discovering its music for the first time, this 30th anniversary celebration is a chance to experience one of animation's most distinctive and enduring scores performed live by the composer who created it.

Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul.

One of international cinema’s greatest stars of the era, Gong Li is “nuanced and understated” (Chicago Reader) as the stifled young woman forced into a repressive world of concubinage. Newly restored, the film stands as one of the defining works of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and international film of the 1990s.

events.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown (35mm)
events.description:
This fast-paced celebration of hysteria put Almodóvar on the map by joyfully parading his depthless obsession with women – especially the wild ones. Driven to the brink by her married lover, Pepa (Carmen Maura) cries at work, lights her bed on fire, and loads the gazpacho with barbiturates. Her girlfriends don’t fare much better in this melodramatic farce that runs at a constant parody-level soap-operatic pitch. It’s no small coincidence that during filming Carmen Maura grew so angry with the director she outright refused to speak to him. Men drive the women of this movie to crisis – a trash collector, Shiite terrorists, boyfriends, Antonio Banderas – and the women fight back as a series of peculiar coincidences tightens the social fabric of Madrid. “I thought this only happened in the movies,” a cab driver tells Pepa after she has him tail another cab. Yeah yeah, her expression says, but it’s headed somewhere very interesting.

events.title: Indigenous Voices: Joey Clift and Terria Smith in conversation
events.description:
Join us as we close out our Native American Heritage Month series, welcoming Joey Clift and Terria Smith to share their latest works — We've Been Here The Whole Time! and I Love You So Many.

Free to attend — RSVP required to reserve your seat.

Speakers
Joey Clift is a Los Angeles-based, Peabody and 2x Emmy Award-nominated comedian, writer, director, producer and enrolled member of the Cowlitz Indian Tribe.
Joey attended college to become a local TV weather person because as a kid he didn’t see any Native American comedians on television, and that made him believe he wasn’t allowed to work in comedy. Since then he has learned that this is not true – and his comedy style reflects that. Joey’s work has been featured in The Washington Post, Pitchfork, NPR, Dead Meat, Dropout and Comedy Central.

Terria Smith is a tribal member of the Torres Martinez Desert Cahuilla Indians and a proud original Californian. She is the editor of News from Native California magazine and director of the Berkeley Roundhouse, Heyday’s California Indian publishing program. Smith is also the editor of the 2023 anthology Know We Are Here: Voices of Native California Resistance. She received her undergraduate degree at Cal Poly Humboldt (formerly Humboldt State University) and earned her master’s degree at the UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism. She lives on her ancestral homelands in the Coachella Valley with her puppy Havana.

events.description:
Tradition meets revolution in Opera San José’s new production of Fiddler on the Roof. In a vibrant Jewish shtetl on the eve of upheaval, Tevye, the enduring dairyman, grapples with his daughters’ dreams of love while clinging to the customs that provide his world’s structural integrity.

In one of America’s most diverse immigrant hubs, this story of heritage, adaptation and belonging is deeply personal, a reflection of San Jose’s own balancing act between honoring the past and stepping bravely into the future.

events.description:
Marin Shakespeare Company presents The Secret Garden, adapted by Jon Tracy from Frances Hodgson Burnett’s beloved novel and directed by Jennifer Le Blanc.
After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.
Five performers create the world of the house, the moor, and the garden through movement, song, and sound. This faithful yet freshly illuminated adaptation honors the wonder of Burnett’s story while making room for each person to grow on their own terms.
A family production especially suited to school-age children, teens, and adults, The Secret Garden offers warmth and wonder alongside themes of parental loss, grief, isolation, and disability.

events.title: Tower of Power
events.venue: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
events.address: 50 Mark West Springs Road, Santa Rosa, CA, 95403
events.description:
For 58 years, Tower of Power has delivered the best in funk and soul music. East Bay Grease defined their sound and landed them with Warner Brothers. Bump City, their 1972 debut for the label, was a hit on both the Billboard 200 and the R&B Albums. The 70s were a boom period with radio classics like “So Very Hard to Go” and “What Is Hip,” and the band continued to tour and record over the years. Fifty years later, in 2018, they returned to Oakland to celebrate their landmark 50th anniversary. Tower’s window-rattling grooves and raucous party spirit had been a balm for the soul throughout their half-century existence.

The band has traveled the world, enjoying hit singles on their own and backing legendary artists, including Otis Redding, Elton John, Santana, the Grateful Dead, John Lee Hooker, Aerosmith, Bonnie Raitt, and countless others. In the process they’ve defined an “Oakland soul” sound as instantly recognizable as those from Castillo’s hometown, Detroit, as well as inspirations like Memphis and Philadelphia.

events.title: Laurie Lewis
events.description:
PHOTO Irene Young

Berkeley’s own Laurie Lewis will be returning to the Freight after last year’s hiatus for her annual Concert of Gratitude. She will be joined by Right Hands Brandon Godman on fiddle and Hasee Ciaccio on bass, along with some very special guests, picking old and recent gems from her vast catalog.

Multi-Granmy nominee Laurie Lewis is a forebear and contemporary of so many bluegrass, old-time, and folk greats. Over more than fifty years in music she has established herself as a truly singular voice, instrumentalist, and frontwoman in genres that lionize tradition, “authenticity,” and emulation.

O California!, releases Spring 2026, is a collection of songs that explore our places in the natural world and in each other’s hearts. The recording process was a truly collaborative and joyful experience between Laurie Lewis and her bandmates Brandon Godman, George Guthrie and Hasee Ciaccio. The album features five new originals from Laurie, five traditional songs (some with new lyrics), and the beautiful "Sweet South Anna River,” from the pen of bluegrass trailblazer and mentor Alice Gerrard.

events.description:
Stay Out

Stay Out is a high-energy punk rock band from Oakland, California, rooted deep in the East Bay DIY scene and driven by a relentless commitment to authenticity, connection, and explosive live performance. Formed in the summer of 2016 by Grant Pack and Mason McGeorge, the band quickly established itself as a force in underground punk- blending raw, aggressive energy with undeniably catchy hooks and melodic sensibility.

Fronted by the dual-vocal attack of Pack and McGeorge, Stay Out delivers a dynamic balance of grit and charisma, pairing blistering riffs with anthemic choruses that hit just as hard in a packed venue as they do through speakers. The lineup was solidified in 2018 with the addition of drummer Nate Reynoso, whose impact on the band’s songwriting and sound helped push their evolution into something sharper, louder, and more cohesive.

Drawing from the legacy of Bay Area punk while carving out their own lane, Stay Out fuses high-octane punk rock with pop-punk accessibility, creating music that’s both chaotic and emotionally resonant. Their lyrics tap into themes of defiance, isolation, struggle, and social tension—reflecting real experiences while maintaining an undercurrent of resilience and unity. Known for their wild, unpredictable live shows and DIY ethos, Stay Out has built their reputation from the ground up—handling everything from recording and production to booking, merch, and promotion independently.

events.description:
In a small town by the sea lives five year old Sosuke, high on a cliff overlooking the Inland Sea. One morning while playing on the rocky beach below his house, he discovers a goldfish he names Ponyo, her head stuck in a jam jar. Sosuke rescues Ponyo and keeps her in a green plastic bucket. Both Ponyo and Sosuke are fascinated by each other and promise to stay firm friends until Ponyos father, a sorcerer who lives deep under the sea, forces her to return with him to the ocean depths. What follows is an amazing underwater adventure for all ages...

PONYO is a substantially lighter and smaller in scope feature when compared to Miyazakis previous two works. The

film was completed entirely using traditional hand-drawn animation, primarily in order to showcase the quality of the

artwork by art director Noboru Yoshida as well as celebrating the innocence and cheerfulness of a childs universe.

Erik Walker * Bill Leigh * PHUONIEX * Sonny Boy Daniel * David Kesler

events.title: New People: An Eye for an Eye
events.description:
This screening will take place at NEW PEOPLE CINEMA, located at 1746 Post Street in Japantown.

Director Tanaz Eshaghian in person for a post-screening Q&A

An Eye for an Eye unfolds like a real-life courtroom thriller, with stakes as high as life and death. Years after killing her abusive husband in an act of self-defense, Tahereh now faces execution unless she can pay the Diya—blood money demanded by her abuser’s family. With the clock ticking and public sympathy running low, her son Mohsen is thrust into a desperate race against time to save his mother’s life, turning to outside donors in a society where victims of domestic abuse are often met with silence—or scorn. With unprecedented access to private negotiations, legal proceedings, and intimate family moments, the filmmakers bring us deep inside a harrowing moral and legal labyrinth. We witness not only the emotional toll on Tahereh and her children, but also the chilling mechanics of a justice system shaped by patriarchal values and religious law. Gripping and deeply human, An Eye for an Eye lays bare the personal costs of systemic injustice—and the fierce resilience of a family fighting for their right to move forward.

events.title: Tokyo Godfathers (Subtitled)
events.description:
Presented in Japanese with English subtitles

In modern-day Tokyo, three homeless people’s lives are changed forever when they discover a baby girl at a garbage dump on Christmas Eve. As the New Year fast approaches, these three forgotten members of society band together to solve the mystery of the abandoned child and the fate of her parents. Along the way, encounters with seemingly unrelated events and people force them to confront their own haunted pasts, as they learn to face their future, together.

Co-written by Keiko Nobumoto (Cowboy Bebop) and featuring a whimsical score by Keiichi Suzuki, TOKYO GODFATHERS is a masterpiece by turns heartfelt, hilarious, and highly original, a tale of hope and redemption in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds. (GKIDS)

TRASH & TREASURES presents:

BEGOTTEN

When it debuted in 1989, E. Elias Merhige’s Begotten fascinated and shocked those who witnessed it. Never before had the screen depicted such a primal, existential drama, and it became one of the must-see films of the 1990s. The intervening decades have not diminished the power of this unique motion picture experience. This new 4K restoration reveals the full photographic body of Begotten, preserving its otherworldly organic texture and retaining its visceral impact, a previously unknown life form captured in cinematic amber.

events.title: Naza
events.description:
NAZA is also playing at NEW PEOPLE

In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them.

Directors Note:

We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanisation of another?

What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

– Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

“An essential, devastating documentary…there’s no turning away from what’s said, you simply can’t unknow what you have heard” – Nicolas Rapold, Sight and Sound...

events.title: Fatherland
events.description:
FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller) – actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

With FATHERLAND, director Paweł Pawlikowski picks up where he left off with his award-winning IDA and COLD WAR, exploring – in his elliptic, distilled style – the themes of identity, family, love and guilt amid the turmoil and confusion of post-war Europe.

“Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master” – Time Out

“A rich and moving journey through post-World War II Germany” – TheWrap

Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul.

One of international cinema’s greatest stars of the era, Gong Li is “nuanced and understated” (Chicago Reader) as the stifled young woman forced into a repressive world of concubinage. Newly restored, the film stands as one of the defining works of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and international film of the 1990s.

Small Town Gay Bar
Hosted by Peaches Christ w/ special guest Director Malcolm Ingram
Tuesday, December 1 | The Castro

Two decades ago, director Malcolm Ingram shined a beautiful, raw, and deeply moving spotlight on the resilience of LGBTQ+ communities in the Deep South with his groundbreaking documentary, Small Town Gay Bar. This year, we are bringing it back to San Francisco’s most iconic silver screen.

Small Town Gay Bar is a tribute to the resiliency of gays living in rural areas throughout America. A moving portrait of men and women fighting to create and maintain community for themselves in the face of great opposition, hypocrisy and prejudice in a largely ignored subculture of discreet backdoor entrances and hushed sexual expression in small town Mississippi.

Experience the film like never before with a gorgeous, brand-new 4K restoration print that captures every ounce of heart, struggle, and triumph in crystal-clear definition. Following the screening, Peaches will sit down with special guest director Malcolm Ingram for an exclusive, live Q&A diving deep into the legacy of the film, behind-the-scenes secrets, and how the landscape of queer safe spaces has evolved over the last twenty years.

Don’t miss this rare opportunity to celebrate queer history, cinema, and community at the Castro Theatre!

events.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown (35mm)
events.description:
Part of IN THE MOOD FOR ALMODÓVAR, presented in anticipation of our upcoming run of BITTER CHRISTMAS.

This fast-paced celebration of hysteria put Almodóvar on the map by joyfully parading his depthless obsession with women – especially the wild ones. Driven to the brink by her married lover, Pepa (Carmen Maura) cries at work, lights her bed on fire, and loads the gazpacho with barbiturates. Her girlfriends don’t fare much better in this melodramatic farce that runs at a constant parody-level soap-operatic pitch. It’s no small coincidence that during filming Carmen Maura grew so angry with the director she outright refused to speak to him.

Men drive the women of this movie to crisis – a trash collector, Shiite terrorists, boyfriends, Antonio Banderas – and the women fight back as a series of peculiar coincidences tightens the social fabric of Madrid. “I thought this only happened in the movies,” a cab driver tells Pepa after she has him tail another cab. Yeah yeah, her expression says, but it’s headed somewhere very interesting.

events.title: Santacon
events.description:
In attendance for a special post-film Q&A will be original Santas John Law and Rob Schmitt, as well as other surprise guests.

Today, Santacon is known as perhaps the single most hated event on the planet. A dreaded day in which tens of thousands of drunk idiots dress like Santa and invade countless cities around the world to live out their drunkest and most violent instincts.

But it began as something else entirely: A piece of absurdism designed to shock people out of their everyday existence by creating a sense of awe and confusion.

Born from the San Francisco underground, the folks who started Santacon in the ’90s are the same people who started Burning Man and who served as the real-life inspiration for Fight Club and Project Mayhem. And today, they want nothing to do with their Christmas creation.

Join us for a special screening of SANTACON, a new documentary from director Seth Porges (Class Action Park). Told with exclusive access to the event’s original creators and with countless hours of never-before-seen home movies from the 1990s, you’ll be transported back in time to a world of awe, wonder, and endless possibility.

All Santas are invited to attend in costume.

Don’t think ELF is one of the best holiday films ever? You sit on a throne of lies!

Christmas movies come and go, but few join the pantheon of the greats. You know the ones – A CHRISTMAS STORY, IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE, and MIRACLE ON 34TH STREET. Jeremiah Chiu is a synthesist in the broadest sense of the word—a craftsperson of the modular synth and other musical instruments and tools, as well as an artist, designer, and educator whose work continually brings disparate forms of knowledge into new relationships. While widely recognized for his versatile electronic music as a solo artist, textured recordings in a duo with violist Marta Sofia Honer, and the experimental quintet he co-leads, SML, Chiu has simultaneously maintained a practice as a graphic designer and visual artist, developing a practice attentive to both the structure of technological systems and the contingencies of liveness and emergence.

For Chiu, visual thinking and musical thinking are not separate disciplines but different expressions of the same innate compositional sensibility. This point of view is born equally from his idiosyncratic sense of aesthetics and his capacity for a warm and porous exchange within a thriving community of creative collaborators that stretches between Chicago and Los Angeles.

Rooted in Chicago's deeply interconnected experimental music community, his music has consistently developed through long-term collaborations and shared artistic inquiry. SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

Para mas información sobre El Grupo, llama al 415-632-9722.

_____

Our support group, El Grupo, has been a stable source of family and community for Latinos, Latinas and their families since the early 1980s. Join us for information about sexual health and harm reduction, meals and social support, and help finding health and social services.

Meetings are in-person at 940 Howard St Group Room A every Thursday from 3 to 5 pm.

Marin Shakespeare Company presents The Secret Garden, adapted by Jon Tracy from Frances Hodgson Burnett’s beloved novel and directed by Jennifer Le Blanc.
After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.
Five performers create the world of the house, the moor, and the garden through movement, song, and sound. This faithful yet freshly illuminated adaptation honors the wonder of Burnett’s story while making room for each person to grow on their own terms.
A family production especially suited to school-age children, teens, and adults, The Secret Garden offers warmth and wonder alongside themes of parental loss, grief, isolation, and disability.

Participants will learn how to make plants such as poinsettias, holly and Christmas cacti in paper for card giving or December-themed botanical art pieces.

No drawing or art experience is necessary to get a great result with this technique which invites cutting and tracing. We'll cover color mixing with watercolors and discuss how a limited color palette can achieve a unified result as well as composition and best practices for clean gluing. All art making materials are provided!

Participants should feel confident handling an X-Acto blade; parents of any children under 14 will be required to sign a waiver.

The past three decades have written a story packed full of surreal experiences, epic moments, groundbreaking involvement and huge accomplishments. The String Cheese Incident has been recognized for their commitment to musical creativity and integrity, for their community spirit, philanthropic endeavors, and for their innovative approach to the business of music.

When The String Cheese Incident’s growth first started gaining momentum in the 1990s, as the Internet was just beginning to take hold and the major-label business model was failing, the band decided to make music on their own terms.

Since then, The String Cheese Incident has gone on to carve out a completely unique approach to the business of music; they are truly pioneers of a new way of “making a band.” With the Internet as their tool, SCI was among the first artists to disseminate information online, such as tour dates, release information, and other news, to their growing fan base. Rather than doing business on such terms as “the bottom line,” SCI put their music and their fans first, opening companies of their own, including a ticketing company, a merchandise company and a fan travel agency, to best serve their community. Director Rafael Manuel in person for a post screening Q&A.

The Philippines’ official submission for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards

Presented by FiliKula

Amid stifling heat and pervasive drought, Isabel (Jorrybell Agoto), a 17-year-old Ilokana from the rural north, works at a posh country club outside Manila, lining up golf balls for powerful men to drive into the verdant horizon. New to the job, she wanders the immaculate grounds sampling its luxuries as members, including an industrialist and his expatriate niece, the club president and his pampered wife, and a slew of Chinese tourists, engage in a complex dance with the club’s doting and subservient staff. But something is rotting beneath the pristine fairways of the elite resort, as Isabel discovers when she tries to return a mislaid golf club to its patriarchal director, Dr. Palanca (Teroy Guzman). The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines, and her own past..

“A masterwork…with Filipiñana, Manuel opens new vistas in the future of the cinema.” – The New Yorker

events.description:
The Crooked Jades

(10th Album Release Show with Special Guest Bruce Kaphan)

A San Francisco original, The Crooked Jades celebrate their 10th studio album release Beautiful World—a culmination of three decades of music-making and surprising musical influences. Pioneers in bringing old-time music to contemporary audiences, The Crooked Jades continue to evolve their unique sound by exploring the roots of Americana, while pushing boundaries and blurring genres. Their fiery and soulful live performances, punctuated with eclectic vintage instrumentation, are full of unexpected sounds and are sure to get audiences on their feet.

Our new album Beautiful World is a musical adventure in time from the 1880's to the1980's! In keeping with our reputation for our embracing diverse musical influences this album presents some surprising genre-blending tracks. Along with the driving fiddle tunes and traditional ballads that we are known for, we reimagined songs culled from the soundtracks of our own lives though the lens of old time music. We can't wait to share this music alchemy with you!

The core of The Crooked Jades are co-founders Jeff Kazor (vocals/guitar/ukulele), Lisa Berman (vocals / slide guitar / banjo / harmonium), and Erik Pearson (vocals / banjos / ukulele / harmonium / slide guitar.) Solo pianist Holly Bowling is an artist who repeatedly defies convention, breaks ceilings, and eludes simplistic labels, while bringing virtuosic playing, emotional immersion, and a thirst for invention to everything that she does. Acclaimed by Rolling Stone and having jammed with a long list of impressive company (Phil Lesh, Bob Weir, Jim James, Warren Haynes, John Scofield, Branford Marsalis, and many more), Holly has established herself as a virtuoso pianist with her own musical voice.

Instagram

Sam Grisman is a bass player, music appreciator, and bandleader who grew up in Mill Valley, California in a home where some of the great acoustic music of our time was being recorded on a regular basis. His father, legendary mandolinist, composer, and producer, David Grisman, was constantly having friends come over to his home studio for recording sessions and rehearsals. These friends, such as Doc Watson, Jerry Garcia, John Hartford, Mike Seeger, and Tony Rice all left an impression on the younger Grisman and inspired him to pursue a life making music with his many talented friends. Sam Grisman Project was created to shed light on the music that Sam grew up around, and highlight that music’s influence on the members of the collective and in the greater music community.

The past three decades have written a story packed full of surreal experiences, epic moments, groundbreaking involvement and huge accomplishments. The String Cheese Incident has been recognized for their commitment to musical creativity and integrity, for their community spirit, philanthropic endeavors, and for their innovative approach to the business of music.

When The String Cheese Incident’s growth first started gaining momentum in the 1990s, as the Internet was just beginning to take hold and the major-label business model was failing, the band decided to make music on their own terms.

Since then, The String Cheese Incident has gone on to carve out a completely unique approach to the business of music; they are truly pioneers of a new way of “making a band.” With the Internet as their tool, SCI was among the first artists to disseminate information online, such as tour dates, release information, and other news, to their growing fan base. Rather than doing business on such terms as “the bottom line,” SCI put their music and their fans first, opening companies of their own, including a ticketing company, a merchandise company and a fan travel agency, to best serve their community. events.description:
As Tycho, Scott Hansen blends swirling melodies into vaguely triumphant arcs that crisscross between stuttering beats and vocal samples, creating rolling sonic landscapes that extend into the horizon. The San Francisco based Hansen began releasing music in the early 2000’s with The Science of Patterns EP. His first full-length, Sunrise Projector, came out in 2004, and the critical acclaim continued in 2006 with the release of Past Is Prologue. In 2011 with the addition of collaborator and guitarist Zac Brown, Hansen’s meticulous process saw the release of Dive, the first record in a trilogy that was followed by Awake in 2014 and the GRAMMY-Nominated Epoch in 2016, two albums that featured Rory O’Connor on drums. Hansen expanded the scope of his project with the addition of vocalist Saint Sinner on 2019’s Weather, Tycho’s second GRAMMY nomination for Best Dance/Electronic Album. That release was quickly followed by its instrumental companion record Simulcast, a collaboration with alt-R&B artist rum.gold and the Weather Remixes project all in 2020. In addition to his original works, Tycho has remixed Odesza & Leon Bridges, Maggie Rogers, Spoon, The Knocks & Muna, Little Dragon, Thievery Corporation and Death Cab For Cutie.

it’s murph

it’s murph is a Nashville-based electronic producer crafting dance music that’s meant to be felt as much as it’s heard. Rooted in emotion but built for movement, his sound lives at the intersection of euphoric melody, gritty low-end, and expansive atmosphere — pulling listeners into moments that feel both intimate and anthemic.

Driven by the belief that music is a multi-sensory experience, it’s murph creates records designed to unlock something deeper: a memory, a feeling, a shared release on the dancefloor. His productions balance warmth and edge, pairing melodic progressions with driving grooves that keep crowds locked in while leaving space to breathe.

Blending influences from tech house, bass-forward dance, and melodic electronic music, his sound draws inspiration from artists like Fred again.., Cloonee, and Chris Lake, while remaining distinctly his own. Whether in headphones or under strobe lights, it’s murph’s music invites listeners to step outside themselves and fully immerse in the moment.

As his catalog continues to grow, it’s murph is carving out a lane defined by emotional energy, forward-thinking production, and a deep connection to the people on the other side of the speakers.

events.title: Haunted Hearth: Paxton Gate’s 34th Annual Holiday Party
events.description:
It’s back! Our annual holiday party is on the books, and you’re all invited. Why are we throwing a party, you may ask? Are we just big fans of the holiday season? Well, yes, but we’re also celebrating Paxton Gate’s 34th anniversary. This year, we’re leaning into the slightly darker folklore surrounding the holiday season (hence the Haunted Hearth theme), and we’ve asked a very special someone to join us. More on that later.
Somehow, 34 years of Paxton Gate is just as mind-blowing to us as 33 was. That’s 34 years of bringing oddities, fossils, minerals, plants, and all sorts of other “Wait, what is that?” stuff to Valencia Street. As jazzed as we are to keep doing what we do, we really couldn’t do any of it without you, our super rad customers and neighbors up and down Valencia Street.
To show y’all just how much we appreciate you, we throw an annual holiday party, and we’d love for you to attend. We’ll have drinks, finger foods, live music, and this year, a very special horned, legendary, and somewhat horrifying guest. Don’t worry, though. He’s promised not to hit anyone with his bundle of birch branches. Why he insists on carrying those around is anyone’s guess.
Anyways, join us for a night of merrymaking, holiday cheer, and hanging out with a demon summoned from the depths of the North Pole.
We’ll see y’all there.

In South Boston, the state police force is waging war on Irish-American organized crime. Young undercover cop Billy Costigan (Leonardo DiCaprio) is assigned to infiltrate the mob syndicate run by gangland chief Frank Costello (Jack Nicholson). While Billy quickly gains Costello's confidence, Colin Sullivan (Matt Damon), a hardened young criminal who has infiltrated the state police as an informer for the syndicate, is rising to a position of power in the Special Investigation Unit. Each man becomes deeply consumed by his double life, gathering information about the plans and counter-plans of the operations he has penetrated. But when it becomes clear to both the mob and the police that there's a mole in their midst, Billy and Colin are suddenly in danger of being caught and exposed to the enemy – and each must race to uncover the identity of the other man in time to save himself. But is either willing to turn on the friends and comrades they've made during their long stints undercover?

Merry Mozart
events.description:
Journey to a place where personal expression and timeless beauty meet in radiant harmony as three composers reveal their most poetic and expressive selves.

Written as a birthday gift for his wife and first performed on Christmas morning, Richard Wagner’s Siegfried Idyll is a rare glimpse of the gentler side of the composer. Filled with tenderness and intimacy, the work is an idyllic unfolding of glowing harmonies, pastoral, calm, and deeply personal affection.

Ottorino Respighi’s Trittico Botticelliano brings three Renaissance paintings to vivid musical life. Inspired by Botticelli’s La Primavera, The Adoration of the Magi, and The Birth of Venus, Respighi’s orchestration shimmers with color and imagination, transforming visual beauty into sound that is refined, atmospheric, and richly evocative.

Mozart’s Symphony No. 39 is a work of noble warmth and exuberant invention. Majestic yet playful, the symphony balances ceremonial grandeur with lyric elegance, offering music that sparkles with clarity, wit, and humanity.

events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Dagmar Zuniga

Nicaraguan-American artist Dagmar Zuniga makes music that feels both intimate and expansive: songs drift like disrupted signals, carried by harmony, tape hiss, and a strong sense of touch. Her debut solo album in filth your mystery is kingdom / far smile peasant in yellow music — written and recorded in New York, Norway, and Athens, Georgia over a period of five years on her longtime companion, the Tascam 424 — was released by the People’s Coalition of Tandy on Bandcamp & YouTube in January 2025, accompanied by a small tape run that sold out instantly. The project quickly garnered over two hundred thousand views and the attention of artists such as Mount Eerie, who invited her to tour with them that summer.

This year, what was once a jewel of tapped-in algorithms and message boards will meet the world at large, with in filth arriving digitally on March 4, and physically on April 10, via AD 93.

in filth is an atmospheric, devotional collage where one voice multiplies into a chorus of selves, sometimes delicate, sometimes severe; an effect created by Zuniga’s masterful layering of texture and complex harmonies. Synths glitter out like spears of sunlight from beneath clouds of moody, time-distorted guitars, and songs spin about themselves like tightly-wound music boxes, making use of a kind of hypnotic repetition, before melting apart into their components or slipping into the following track.

events.description:
Circle Jerks (stylized as Ciʀcle JƎʀᴋs) are an American hardcore punk band, formed in 1979 in Los Angeles, California. The group was founded by former Black Flag vocalist Keith Morris and Redd Kross guitarist Greg Hetson. To date, Circle Jerks have released six studio albums, one compilation, a live album and a live DVD. Their debut album, Group Sex (1980), is considered a landmark of the hardcore genre.

The band has broken up and re-formed several times, sometimes with different bassists and/or drummers. They disbanded for the first time after the release of their fifth album VI (1987), allowing Hetson to focus on Bad Religion (where he had been a member from 1984 to 2013) full-time. The Circle Jerks first reunited in 1994 and released their sixth and last studio album to date, Oddities, Abnormalities and Curiosities, the following year before separating for the second time. The band reunited for the second time in 2001 and spent the next ten years performing live periodically; this reunion lasted for only one new song, "I'm Gonna Live", which was released on their MySpace profile in 2007. Tensions among its members and failed attempts to record the follow-up to Oddities, Abnormalities and Curiosities resulted in the Circle Jerks breaking up yet again in 2011. However, the band announced in November 2019 that they will reunite in 2020 to celebrate the 40th anniversary of Group Sex with live shows.
