events.title: London
events.description: Bobby drives back and forth on the highway that links Vienna and Salzburg to visit his friend who is in a coma. He picks up other travellers to save money on petrol including the soldier questioning what it means to fight, the supermarket trainee heading to see family, the academic looking at the history of the highway, the queer woman about to get married—different paths, different accents, different stories, most of them true. Mountains and forests rush by outside, broken up by junctions, barriers and bridges, the quality of light shifts along with the seasons. Neither a documentary, nor entirely fiction, London is a quietly political portrait of today's Europe via its in-between spaces and those passing through them.

events.title: Merry Mozart
events.description:
Journey to a place where personal expression and timeless beauty meet in radiant harmony as three composers reveal their most poetic and expressive selves.

Written as a birthday gift for his wife and first performed on Christmas morning, Richard Wagner’s Siegfried Idyll is a rare glimpse of the gentler side of the composer. Filled with tenderness and intimacy, the work is an idyllic unfolding of glowing harmonies, pastoral, calm, and deeply personal affection.

Ottorino Respighi’s Trittico Botticelliano brings three Renaissance paintings to vivid musical life. Inspired by Botticelli’s La Primavera, The Adoration of the Magi, and The Birth of Venus, Respighi’s orchestration shimmers with color and imagination, transforming visual beauty into sound that is refined, atmospheric, and richly evocative.

Mozart’s Symphony No. 39 is a work of noble warmth and exuberant invention. Majestic yet playful, the symphony balances ceremonial grandeur with lyric elegance, offering music that sparkles with clarity, wit, and humanity.

Stephen Steinbrink

(Record Release Show)

Stephen Steinbrink (b. 1988) is a songwriter, producer, and visual artist. Immersing himself in the West Coast underground DIY community in the mid-2000s, Steinbrink left on his first tour at the age of sixteen and continued performing internationally for a decade, living an improvised existence and recording incessantly. He has released nine critically acclaimed albums of experimental pop music and has collaborated as a producer and session player with artists including Boy Scouts/Taylor Vick, Dear Nora, Gia Margaret, LAKE, and Girlpool.

Though appearing luminous and graceful on the surface, his songs use the recognizable logic of pop structures as a container for psychic inquiry, revealing the unstable landscapes of memory, dreams, and the quotidian absurdities of daily life. Over two decades, Steinbrink has become one of the most distinctive songwriters on the U.S. West Coast, with a rarely matched gift for poetic imagery carried by a musical language that moves across folk, experimental pop, and ambient experimentation.

In visual art, Steinbrink works in illustration, photography, animation, and Stained Glass conservation, having restored historic art glass throughout Northern California. He currently lives and works in Oakland, California.

events.title: Nuisance Bear
events.description:
“Truly groundbreaking” – Werner Herzog

“A David Attenborough doc shot by someone on shrooms.” – i-D Magazine

For thousands of years, polar bears have migrated along the shores of Hudson Bay in northern Canada. Today, that ancient rhythm collides with a human world of tourism, surveillance, and control. Nuisance Bear immerses viewers in the experience of a polar bear forced to navigate tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters as climate change delays the freeze and pushes bears closer to human settlements. When a sacred predator is branded a “nuisance,” it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

Returning to Churchill, Manitoba—the self-styled “Polar Bear Capital of the World”—filmmakers Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman expand their award-winning short into a feature guided by an Inuit narrator whose perspective resists simplification. Shot with striking intimacy and scale, the film observes bears that are constantly monitored, photographed, and redirected. In tracing this uneasy coexistence, Nuisance Bear becomes a meditation on how humans manage, commodify, and redefine wildlife—overturning the conventions of the nature documentary and reframing animals not as spectacle, but as active agents in a rapidly changing world.

events.title: AHITH FEST 2026: Starslyderz
events.description:
20 years later, STARSLYDERZ comes home!

In 2006, a bonkers, no-budget sci-fi comedy called STARSLYDERZ premiered at Another Hole in the Head Film Festival, where Variety boldly declared, “Cult status is assured.”

The film went on to screen at Fantasia and open France's Mauvais Genre Festival before being picked up by a distributor who promptly buried it. When the heartbroken filmmakers finally regained the rights five years later, they made an unusual decision: lock it away and let it age like a fine wine.

Now, 20 years after its original AHITH premiere, STARSLYDERZ returns to the festival where it all began, featuring a newly remastered edit that no audience has ever seen!

Shot guerrilla-style over two chaotic weeks on MiniDV throughout San Francisco, this gloriously unhinged sci-fi adventure features a troupe of sleep-deprived young actors, an army of puppets, the work of approximately 150 volunteer visual effects artists, and an incredible soundtrack featuring Santa Cruz's legendary experimental band Estradasphere.

You've never seen anything quite like STARSLYDERZ.

Join us for this special 20th Anniversary Re-Premiere, with the filmmakers in attendance and a theater full of fellow weirdos!

One film. Twenty years. A whole new level of strange.

You've seen The Shining. You've never seen it like this.

What happens when Stanley Kubrick's legendary horror masterpiece plays forwards and backwards simultaneously, with both versions superimposed over one another?

Faces merge. Hallways intersect. Characters appear to encounter their own past and future. The Overlook Hotel becomes an entirely new labyrinth of visual mysteries.

There's only one way to find out.

events.title: American Psycho
events.description:
“Look at that subtle off-white coloring. The tasteful thickness of it. Oh, my God. It even has a watermark.”

Before Christian Bale was the savior of Gotham, he was the chainsaw-wielding, business card-slinging scourge of Manhattan. Caught during the height of American Yuppieism in the late '80s, Patrick Bateman finds himself surrounded by friends who he hates and a culture he can’t stand. Can anyone blame him for allowing his nightly bloodlust to overflow into the day?

It’s hard to imagine anyone aside from Bale lecturing a soon-to-be victim on the cultural undertones found within Huey Lewis and The News’ “Hip to be Square,” all while wearing a raincoat and holding an incredibly shiny axe. But, what now seems meant to be almost wasn’t! The role was originally offered to none other than Leonardo DiCaprio. However, due to his newfound fame within the teenaged female demographic, Leo’s managers felt that a stint as a sociopathic mass murderer might somehow taint his image. I guess a career in murders and executions isn’t for everyone.

Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have to return some videotapes.

events.description:
The endurance athlete, ocean explorer & storyteller comes to KALW to discuss her landmark journey swimming California's coastline.

Catherine Breed is redefining what modern adventure can look like — where human performance, environmental connection, and community impact meet. Earlier this year, she became the first person to swim the length of California's coast. Join her at KALW on Dec. 9 for an intimate conversation moderated by Ben Trefny, live and in person at our Community Engagement Studio at 220 Montgomery St.

Drawn to the water from an early age, Catherine’s journey began in elite competitive swimming, representing UC Berkeley and the U.S. National Team. Years of disciplined training shaped her understanding of resilience and focus, but her true evolution began when she stepped beyond the structure of the pool and into the vast unpredictability of open water.

In 2016, Catherine found her home within San Francisco’s historic open-water swimming community at the Dolphin Club, where cold water, powerful tides, and a culture of bold exploration challenged her to redefine limits. Surrounded by legendary swimmers and lifelong adventurers, she began pursuing ambitious endurance swims that transformed swimming from competition into exploration — and ultimately into a platform for storytelling and impact.

events.title: 20/20 Vision: Is This the Moment for Smart Glasses?
events.address: 1401 North Shoreline Boulevard, Mountain View, CA, 94043
events.description:
Smart glasses are having a moment, surpassing all other wearables, with rapid market growth and projected revenues of more than $5 billion this year.

A decade ago, smart glasses hadn’t caught on with most consumers. They were expensive, technically limited, impractical for everyday use, and the always-on camera sparked privacy concerns.

This time it looks different. Game-changing technological advances have improved hardware significantly, and AI integration supports hands-free photography, audio translation, navigation, and contextual assistance. Partnerships with fashion brands are turning out stylish frames. To support greater transparency around questions of surveillance and privacy, some designs feature recording indicators, and others omit facial recognition and cameras entirely.

In this CHM Live forum, product leaders from Meta, Google, and Applied Materials unpack the latest technology and human-centered design driving the next generation of smart eyewear.

John Markoff, a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist and former CHM staff historian, will moderate and bring deep historical insight into this conversation about blending digital information with our physical world.

With technology, design and AI finally converging, smart glasses may be entering their most promising chapter yet.

events.description:
Buy Tickets

Curated & presented by Bradford Nordeen in association with Dirty Looks, The Lab and San Francisco Cinematheque

This program was initially organized in collaboration between Dirty Looks and LA Filmforum

This screening is dedicated to Agosto Machado (????–2026)—“a lady never tells.”

Jack Smith was an underground visionary in every sense of the word. Jack poured glitter into everything he made: pasty creatures, plastic fantasias and moldy monsters. He was a performance artist, filmmaker, playwright, photographer, socialist, aesthete, installation artist, scene-stealer, writer, interventionist. He built a theater and movie-studio in his rickety loft out of street debris; an intricate and child-like universe, Cinemaroc, was equal parts Baroque and broke. For a contingency of art and theater fags and dolls, Jack, as Charles Ludlam once eloquently put it, “is the daddy of us all.” And quixotically, the fact that he remains a somewhat underground or cult figure, as opposed to canonized creature, attests to his legacy.

Best known as a filmmaker, Jack made wild, indeterminable pictures. Flaming Creatures was his first finished film. Well, in truth, it’s his only finished film, since it ricocheted out of his hands when a trend of underground film raids made his opus a trophy for either side of a decency debate. Seized at the same time as Jean Genet’s Un chant d’amour (1950) and Kenneth Anger’s Scorpio...

Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes, MINOTAUR is the latest from Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev (LEVIATHAN, LOVELESS). His riveting, razor-sharp tale of personal, patriarchal, and governmental corruption follows a wealthy CEO who begins to suspect his wife is having an extramarital affair. France’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

Now living in exile, Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev has been creating impeccable, trenchant allegories about the moral and political condition of his home country throughout the 21st century, and his latest is one of his most riveting and razor-sharp. Set in 2022 Russia, Minotaur centers on middle-aged businessman Gleb (Dmitry Mazurov), a transport company CEO who lives an ultra-comfortable domestic life with his wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) and teenage son in a sleek modernist home in a private wooded area. As the film begins, he is tasked by the town’s powerful mayor with drafting a quota of his employees to send to the newly ongoing war in Ukraine; at the same time, he begins to suspect that Galina is having an affair, which leads him to take drastic action. With the finesse of his stated inspiration Claude Chabrol, Zvyagintsev has constructed a tale of corruption—personal, patriarchal, and governmental—that slow-burns with rage and fearless dark humor.

Nominated for three 2026 Gotham Film Awards, including Best Director, Best International Feature, and Best Adapted Screenplay.

events.description:
When The Kettle Sings Tour

The Fretliners

Thursday, December 10 | The Freight

There is something happening between the mountains and the plains. A stirring in the dust. A song rising from the timber. Out of that landscape of grit and grace comes The Fretliners, a band carrying forward the oldest tradition in American music: telling the truth.

You can call them Colorado’s next great acoustic act. You can point to their Telluride and RockyGrass New Artist wins. You can talk about their musicianship, their harmonies, or their ability to command a room. All of those things are true. But they only tell part of the story.

The Fretliners are carving their own path through American music, drawing from bluegrass, Americana, folk, and rock to create something that feels both familiar and completely their own. Their songs carry the weight of long roads, changing seasons, lost loves, and the quiet hope that keeps people moving forward.

What separates The Fretliners is not just how they play, but what they have to say. Their writing feels rooted in something older than trends. They sing about places that shaped them, people who stayed, memories that linger, and the moments that remind us we are still connected to something real.

There is a kind of honesty in their music that cannot be manufactured. Each note feels lived-in,like old wood worn smooth by generations of hands. Each lyric feels like a conversation around a fire, a story passed down because it still matters.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Storefront Church
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Storefront Church

Storefront Church is the project of Lukas Frank, who's drummed in Phoebe Bridgers' band and appeared on her albums, and the first song of his debut album As We Pass features DIIV frontman Cole Smith, but neither of those affiliations really prepares you for what to expect from As We Pass. It's a 9-song collection that's largely made up of bluesy, gothy, emo-y melancholic songs that sometimes sound like a cross between '90s Cure deep cuts and Nirvana Unplugged. (Lukas also cites Scott Walker as an influence, and you can hear that too.) Most of the album is bare-bones and somber, but Lukas also revs things up for the noise punk of "Faction from Under the Grove," and that fits right in too. With As We Pass, Lukas enters a long, line of depressive singer/songwriters, but even with over half a century of music like this, something about Lukas stands out. He grips you right off the bat with album opener "After the Alphabets" -- the kind of song that can make you drop everything and listen as soon as his voice comes in -- and the album stays that compelling throughout. Even with connections to established artists and the great Sargent House label behind him, this doesn't feel like the smash arrival of a hot new buzz artist; it's the subtle arrival of a songwriter whose songs creep up on you and knock you out when you're least expecting it. Usually, that's even better.

Lucius

Rooted in mirrored kinship and a captivating vocal blend, Lucius — the Grammy-nominated indie-pop duo of Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig — are songwriters of rare emotional precision, building one of contemporary music’s most enchanting, harmonic sounds. Their voices, described by the Los Angeles Times as “otherworldly,” move in perfect tandem: two instruments so attuned they read as one. Rolling Stone called their most recent album, 2025’s self-titled “the best album of their career” — a distinction earned through hard-won vulnerability, as Wolfe and Laessig turn inward to explore motherhood, relationships, and the quiet complexities of a life shared. The New Yorker wrote that the record “reaches the pinnacle of a vibrant, harmonic enterprise.”

The arc of their catalog is one of continuous, confident evolution. Their debut, Wildewoman, announced a singular voice — dual lead vocals wrapped in retro charm, which The New York Times praised the live show that year as “the best musical performance of any kind.”

Good Grief introduced a sleeker, synth-driven palette, while Second Nature — produced by Brandi Carlile and Dave Cobb — was celebrated by the Los Angeles Times with its “lush synths and sleek disco grooves under the women’s laser-guided vocals.”

events.title: Inspiring Splendor
events.description: This December, the PWC joins forces with the Palo Alto Chamber Orchestra to perform Vivaldi’s beloved Gloria. Carrying forward this season of celebration of women, by women, we’ll perform pieces by several composers who continue to inspire us. In addition to Vivaldi’s masterwork, the second half of our winter program celebrates the season with sacred and contemporary holiday treasures. Experience the luminous anticipation of Elaine Hagenberg’s O Come Emmanuel, Joan Szymko’s spirited Hodie, and Ann Callaway’s radiant Alleluia, Vidimus Stellam, paired with the otherworldly textures of Cindy Cox’s Wakah-Chan. We uplift traditions of community, reflection, and peace through Bernice Johnson Reagon’s stirring Seven Principles and Karen Siegel’s contemplative Oseh Shalom. The festivities draw to a heartwarming close with the gentle tenderness of Eleanor Daley’s Lullaby Carol and the timeless splendor of John Rutter’s setting of Silent Night. Join us 30 minutes before each performance for a pre-concert talk, and stay for a post-concert reception.

events.title: Spike Sikes and His Awesome Hotcakes: Holiday show
events.description:
Just The Right Recipe… The most frequently heard comment after a Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes gig goes something like this –
“No one is making this kind of music anymore!”
But what, exactly, is “this kind of music?”
Like hotcakes themselves, it goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump. It’s a sound that’s classic and simple, but when it’s done right, it hits the spot, and has you grinning from ear to ear. Spike has spent years searching for this sound.
From the Texas blues joints he cut his teeth in to the funky halls of New Orleans, he was always studying the music, trying to find just the right recipe. It makes perfect sense that he found his bandmates in Sonoma County, a music scene that has fostered many eclectic artists for decades.
What he didn’t know was how hungry audiences were for “this kind of music.” You might say they’ve been eating it up like…Hotcakes!

events.title: Fargo Nissim Tbakhi: The Book of Dust
events.description:
Doors 7:30pm / Show 8pm

Free

Small Press Traffic presents The Book of Dust, a solo performance by performance artist and poet Fargo Nissim Tbakhi. First presented in 2024, the work anchors a remarkable run in his practice: it precedes Terror Counter (Deep Vellum, 2025), his debut poetry collection which was longlisted for the National Book Award, and the play EVE, his collaboration with poet George Abraham, recently presented by the Arab American National Museum, Mizna, and Silk Road Cultural Center in August 2026. His next book, Antigone.Velocity. Salt., is forthcoming from Deep Vellum in 2027.

Tbakhi’s script is a cascade of language from source texts including the Book of Job and Archibald MacLeish’s 1950s radio play JB, set within the eviscerating throughline of his own text-monologue addressing impossible mourning in the genocide in Gaza. Using video, interactive elements, and sparse staging, The Book of Dust advances a ruthless examination of the ways Palestinian speech, suffering, life, and death are digested and constricted by global power structures. In this hour-long meditation on grief, Tbakhi interrogates the limits of performance and witness, asking audiences to sit with despair, complicity, horror, and shame.

Fargo Nissim Tbakhi is a Palestinian performance artist and the author of TERROR COUNTER (Deep Vellum, 2025) and ANTIGONE. VELOCITY. SALT. (Deep Vellum, 2027).

events.title: Understanding Attachment Trauma & Building Resilience with Mindfulness
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Pawan Bareja, PhD and Diane Poole Heller
We begin life with a child’s open heart, full of trust, innocence, and pure joy. Yet, over time, the world leaves its marks. We often arrive at our meditation cushions carrying a lifetime of hidden grief, from the lingering ache of a breakup to the quiet sorrow of a loveless childhood. To protect ourselves from this attachment trauma, we build walls that close us off from the very people we wish to love.
This daylong is an invitation to return home to the pure love that is your true nature. We do not heal in isolation; we heal together. Our nervous systems are beautifully social, wired to find safety, warmth, and co-regulation in the presence of others.
If accepting love feels foreign, you can break those protective patterns. Through guided meditations, gentle reflection, and supportive group connections, we will mend broken bonds, navigate love and conflict, and rebuild our lasting resilience.
Diane will lead a practical teaching session drawing on her background in nervous-system-informed approaches to attachment, offering an embodied complement to the day’s content.

events.title: Eyes Wide Shut
events.description:
In IT’S A WONDERFUL LIFE, Jimmy Stewart’s George Bailey, at the height of his suicidal despair and panic, imagines a world in which he doesn’t exist. Stanley Kubrick goes one step further in sending Tom Cruise down an odyssey of sexual confusion and paranoia to learn the true meaning of Christmas.

Adapted from the Austrian short story Traumnovelle, Kubrick’s final film peeks us into the privileged world of Dr. Bill Hartford and his wife Alice (Cruise and Nicole Kidman), two well-to-do attractive socialites who, by all accounts, have it made. In a marijuana-fueled argument, Alice reveals thoughts of infidelity that send Bill into an existential panic, leading to an absurdist walkabout through New York that involves – you guessed it – a mysterious sex cult run by a shrouded aristocracy.

Did Kubrick make this to break up Cruise and Kidman’s marriage? How much did he know about mysterious sex trafficking rings? Did Sydney Pollack originate the shirtless-in-suspenders look? Clearly, the film poses more questions than it answers. For certain, EYES WIDE SHUT is a brutally funny sexscapade that puts an ellipses at the end of Kubrick’s storied career – and, most importantly – stands as a crucial text for our modern world. Fidelio!

events.description: This December, the PWC joins forces with the Palo Alto Chamber Orchestra to perform Vivaldi’s beloved Gloria. In addition to Vivaldi’s masterwork, the second half of our winter program celebrates the season with sacred and contemporary holiday treasures. Experience the luminous anticipation of Elaine Hagenberg’s O Come Emmanuel, Joan Szymko’s spirited Hodie, and Ann Callaway’s radiant Alleluia, Vidimus Stellam, paired with the otherworldly textures of Cindy Cox’s Wakah-Chan. The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own.

She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition.

She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for.

Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive....

events.title: Little Women (2019)
events.description:
Having already once revolutionized the coming-of-age story with her debut LADY BIRD, Greta Gerwig has somehow outdone herself with this gorgeous and thoroughly original rendition of the beloved Louisa May Alcott classic. Bringing her effusive humor, authenticity, and irresistible warmth to the otherwise mannered Civil War-era New England, Gerwig's adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN breathes visceral new life into the March sisters – portraying them as unique, complicated, flawed, and astonishingly human. So human that you will leave the theater wanting to text Jo March and, for several reasons, this will not be a possibility.

You may also find it physically impossible not to chef's kiss at the cast, which is as close to pitch-perfect as it gets. Starring Saoirse Ronan as Jo, Emma Watson as Meg, Florence Pugh as Amy, and Eliza Scanlen as Beth, LITTLE WOMEN also features Laura Dern (!), Meryl Streep (!), Bob Odenkirk (!), and Timothée Chalamet as the dashing but lovelorn Laurie (!!!).

Save for a fireworks show, sky-written ode, or Mount Rushmore-type situation, we cannot recommend this rich, heartrending wonder of a film anymore. Its timeless charm is sure to capture the hearts of little women (and men) everywhere.

events.title: AHITH FEST 2026: The Haunting of Pennhurst
events.description:
At a former institution for people with disabilities, a haunted attraction employs disabled performers who confront the site’s abusive past while reclaiming its story on their own terms.

On the grounds of the former Pennhurst State School and Hospital, where generations of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities endured neglect and abuse, a haunted attraction now draws thousands of visitors each year. But The Haunting of Pennhurst is less interested in cheap scares than in what it means to turn a site of real suffering into entertainment. Following the disabled and neurodivergent performers who bring the attraction to life, the documentary reveals a haunt shaped by unusually deliberate rules. Actors are encouraged to build characters from their own experiences, while slurs, mockery, and violence that recreates historical abuse are strictly off-limits. For some performers, stepping into the role of “monster” becomes an act of reclamation in a place once designed to segregate people like them. Yet the contradictions remain. Archival footage, survivor testimony, and the site’s museum continually return the film to Pennhurst’s brutal history, raising difficult questions about memory, exploitation, education, and who gets to tell the story of a place built on suffering. Immersive and unsettling with an original score by Dan Deacon, the film leaves space for viewers to decide whether Pennhurst’s new life is catharsis, commerce, or something more complicated.

Mrs. Claus & The Naughty Ones transforms a working San Francisco maker space into Mrs. Claus's North Pole workshop for an intimate, immersive Christmas gathering on December 13.

Created by San Francisco artist and immersive-event producer Indy, the evening reimagines Mrs. Claus not simply as Santa's wife, but as the woman running a strange, playful Christmas world of her own.

Approximately 100-125 guests will step inside a functioning holiday workshop populated by Mrs. Claus and her cast of Christmas characters and elves. Throughout the space, guests can decorate cookies, make ornaments, take holiday portraits, share a Christmas meal, and bring new toys for a Toys for Tots drive. Workshop elves will receive, organize and wrap those donated toys throughout the evening, making the charitable drive part of the immersive world itself.

The project blends queer theatricality, character performance, community gathering and immersive design while keeping the scale intentionally intimate. Rather than presenting a traditional stage show, Mrs. Claus & The Naughty Ones invites guests to enter the story and spend an evening inside it.

At the center is a simple reinterpretation of a familiar Christmas figure: Mrs. Claus is no longer merely remembered in relation to Santa. In this workshop, she is the author of her own legend.

events.title: French Café Music dinner concert with Bistro Moustache
events.description:
Bistro Moustache plays French Café music, a style that mixes Manouche, Gypsy Jazz, Musette, Swing, and that was popular in France before and after the Second World War, and that is still very much alive today.

We go from the popular timeless classics (Les Feuilles Mortes, C’est Si Bon, Ménilmontant, J’Attendrai, La Foule, Sous Le Ciel De Paris, La Vie En Rose) to more modern (Il Est Cinq Heures Paris S’Éveille, Le Poinçonneur Des Lilas, Le Déserteur, Vesoul), and even songs that you may hear on the French radio today. We also feature dance tunes, Waltzes, Polkas, Tangos, Auvergne Bourrées and Celtic folk, or French children comptines, like Frère Jacques, or Sur Le Pont D’Avignon. All the songs are sung in French by Olivier, a native Parisian.

Just as if Charles Trenet, Jacques Brel, Yves Montand, Georges Brassens, Serge Gainsbourg, Tino Rossi, Edith Piaf, Boris Vian, Django Reinhardt, Gus Viseur and Jo Privat were all on the same stage together for one evening.

Prepare to be musically transported to the terrace of a Paris Bistro, a Guinguette on the Marne river or a Bal Musette on the banks of the Seine.

More info at: http://www.bistromoustache.com/calendar

events.title: Bitter Christmas
events.description:
Check out IN THE MOOD FOR ALMODÓVAR, our limited series celebrating three earlier works by Pedro Almodóvar.

The incomparable Almodóvar has been rendering the life of the creative mind on screen for five decades, with exquisite attention to every nuance of both aesthetic design and human emotion. With his complexly conceived latest, he uses a metacinematic framework to explore the artist’s tenuous relationship between fiction and reality. The sublimely expressive Bárbara Lennie stars as Elsa, a well-known actress suffering from debilitating migraines whose directorial efforts had failed upon release but have become cult classics. While trying to maintain a relationship with her loyal boyfriend Bonifacio (Patrick Criado), a fireman moonlighting as a stripper, she becomes inspired by the travails of her friends to write a new script.

Yet Elsa’s story is itself a story—being written by Raúl (Leonardo Sbaraglia), an Almodóvar-esque filmmaker who is, in turn, taking his cues from the lives of those around him. Mixing the irreverence of early Almodóvar with the somber melodrama of his later work, Bitter Christmas insightfully details the vampiric nature of artistic creation and how we use fiction to try and right the wrongs of our lives.

“With its moving musical interludes, comic patter and outrageously chic production design, Bitter Christmas is another dazzling, late-period jewel” — Little White Lies

For two decades, Pokey LaFarge has walked his own effortlessly cool road as an exceptionally iconoclastic troubadour – forthright, genuine, and markedly keen to put it all out there. With its twanging guitars, plucky rhythms, and undeniably captivating melodies, the album soars and swings, its joyous refrains belying the inescapable undercurrent of constant worry and angst that permeates these troubled times. As always, the Illinois native deftly traverses the genre boundaries, seamlessly integrating the myriad strains of 20th-century American music with a freewheeling command of earnest songcraft, inspired performance, and subversive creativity. Rent Money stands tall as an indisputable high-water mark for Pokey LaFarge – a defining collection from a one-of-a-kind artist of rare ingenuity and uncommon candor, now as ever, determinedly crafting a sure-footed brand of deeply human music all his own.

Pinpointing the specific catalyst for an avalanche can be slippery — any combination of classic elements, human interference, or freak accident can trigger disaster — and documenting these precise moments often rests on serendipitous reflexes. On Two Wheels Move the Soul, Robber Robber offer themselves as ignition and capture every sound in the wake. Involuntarily thrust into the throws of rootless nomadism, Robber Robber ringleader Nina Cates collects a series of pressurized vignettes to assemble the Burlington quartet’s thrillingly explosive sophomore album.

Two Wheels Move the Soul was written and recorded throughout the winter of 2024 and 2025, a season of Cates’ life characterized by near-constant upheaval. In January of 2025, Cates (and Robber Robber co-founder) Zack James were displaced from their longtime home at the behest of a landlord’s call to have their building demolished. In a moment’s notice — and amidst a particularly brutal Vermont winter — Cates and James were left to fend for themselves. Luckily, the two were able to tap a deep well of support within their community, finding respite on the couches of Lily Seabird, Greg Freeman, and Thus Love’s Echo Mars. Five years after the massacre at Camp Crystal Lake, a new group of young counselors arrives at a nearby training camp, unaware that something sinister is lurking in the surrounding woods. As the bodies begin to pile up, a terrifying new killer emerges from the shadows, carrying on the bloody legacy of Crystal Lake.

Directed by Steve Miner, Friday the 13th Part 2 (1981) is one of the most beloved entries in the legendary horror franchise. Featuring suspenseful kills, an unforgettable final girl, and Jason Voorhees in his original sack-mask appearance, this sequel helped establish the formula that would define slasher cinema throughout the 1980s.

For this special Another Hole in the Head Film Festival screening, we're bringing Jason back to the big screen projected from an authentic vintage 16mm film print. Experience the gritty atmosphere, old-school practical effects, and unmistakable charm of watching a horror classic on real celluloid.

Marin Shakespeare Company presents The Secret Garden, adapted by Jon Tracy from Frances Hodgson Burnett’s beloved novel and directed by Jennifer Le Blanc.
After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.
Five performers create the world of the house, the moor, and the garden through movement, song, and sound. This faithful yet freshly illuminated adaptation honors the wonder of Burnett’s story while making room for each person to grow on their own terms.
A family production especially suited to school-age children, teens, and adults, The Secret Garden offers warmth and wonder alongside themes of parental loss, grief, isolation, and disability.

events.title: AHITH FEST 2026: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre – Presented by Warped VHS + 1 Short Film
events.description:
Before streaming. Before digital. Before horror became polished. There was VHS — and there was Leatherface.

Five friends traveling through rural Texas stumble upon a nightmare beyond imagination when they encounter a seemingly abandoned farmhouse and the terrifying family that calls it home. What begins as an innocent road trip quickly descends into one of the most relentless and disturbing experiences ever captured on film.

Directed by Tobe Hooper, The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (1974) forever changed the face of horror cinema. Shot on a shoestring budget with a raw, documentary-like style, the film shocked audiences worldwide and introduced Leatherface, one of the most iconic villains in movie history. More than 50 years later, its atmosphere of dread, unrelenting tension, and unforgettable imagery remain just as powerful.

For this special Another Hole in the Head Film Festival screening, Warped VHS presents The Texas Chain Saw Massacre straight from VHS tape, projected onto the big screen at the historic Balboa Theater in San Francisco!

Forget pristine digital restorations and razor-sharp 4K. This is horror the old-school way — analog video, tracking imperfections, and all the gritty nostalgia of discovering a forbidden horror classic on a late-night VHS rental.

+ 1 Short Film

No Late Fees (13 Minutes)

Two video rental store employees must face off against an alien threat in search of a specific 90s VHS classic.

Whitney Johnson, Lia Kohl, and Macie Stewart are a trio who utilize string instruments, voices, and manual tape effect processing to craft compositions from alternately tranquil and disquieting improvised music. The three musicians are individually rooted in deep sound exploration, multi-disciplinary composition, and all manner of cross-genre collaboration. The musical ground covered by their solo practices is correspondingly expansive, and their individual recording and performance credits read as a veritable who’s who, ranging from DIY darlings to household names of experimental avant-garde, electronic, indie rock, and more.

Their influences are vast — dispatched with more playful ease than a trio of string instruments is typically approached with, and just as likely to be found in the cloud-obscured mountains of Donegal, the low-rent cacophony of a Midwestern basement, or the revelatory expanse of the Nurse With Wound list as in the storied halls of the academy. Touchstones and areas of interest aside, the main thing that Johnson, Kohl, and Stewart engage with in BODY SOUND is: listening and reacting.

From Academy Award–winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR) comes a moving exploration of time, memory, and human connection.

Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs, whose life takes an unexpected turn when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), a Japanese playwright. As the two women reflect on the lives they’ve lived, they discover new ways to understand the time that remains. Attentive to the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a deeply humane film about the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and connection.

events.description:

After two EPs and an illuminating start to his career, Grammy Award-winning saxophonist Venna releases his debut album, MALIK.

For Venna, it’s been a whirlwind of a journey to arrive at this point. He’s spent the better part of three years on the road touring, while coming back to London intermittently. In the spaces he finds himself in as a musician, he’s often the youngest in the room. This period gave him the confidence to embark on this next stage of his career.

“Every experience, every memory, every conversation, anything new, any encounter has influenced how this album sounds. I might like a particular guitar tone from it, and then I bring it into my world. Everything has come and conjured into one place, and it’s beautiful to also hear and see,” Venna says.

Speaking on how he found the words to sing: “Does anyone really have the words to say? I don’t know. I don’t know if I had the words to say. I just conjured words and thoughts and tried to make art out of it.”

Featuring vocals from Jorja Smith, Cari, Leon Thomas, Smino, MIKE, and himself, MALIK is where listeners can get lost and find themselves again. The album also features a long list of musicians including Rocco Palladino, Elijah Fox, AoD, J Warner, Marco Bernardis and longtime collaborator, Yussef Dayes.

events.description:
Country Risquè

(Special Dolly Parton Tribute feat. Sadie Alan)

Since making their live debut in 2022, Country Risqué has become something of a San Francisco queer country institution. Singer-songwriters Miles Gordon and Daniel Bromfield first met in Eugene, Oregon nearly a decade before forming the band, and after passing around songwriting ideas during the pandemic, they reconvened in San Francisco and formed a honky-tonk band centered around the coffee-and-chocolate contrast of Gordon’s rich, formally trained vocals and Bromfield’s languid deadpan. As the band has developed, its sound has progressed from a classic ‘50s-influenced country style to a rougher and more electrified sound inspired by alt-country, heartland rock and the rugged landscapes of the Pacific Northwest.

Country Risqué has had the privilege of sharing the stage with Lilly Hiatt, Paisley Fields, Ty Walker and the Humanoids, Secret Emchy Society, and countless other country and many other Americana luminaries. It currently features Richard Moog on lead guitar, Chris Kenyon on drums, and Sarah Parker on bass.

events.title: Robert Glasper
events.description:
Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing.

Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu.

Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz...

events.title: Florencia Ramirez, The Kitchen Activist
events.description:
Saturday, December 19, 2026, 11:00 am - 11:45 am

Stop by the Foodwise Classroom for a cooking demo featuring the seasonal bounty of the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market.

Florencia Ramirez is the author of The Kitchen Activist: Your Step-by-Step Guide to Creating a Planet Smart Kitchen and Eat Less Water: The Solution to Water Shortages is in the Kitchen. A storyteller at heart and researcher by training, she holds a masters degree in public policy from the University of Chicago. Through writing, research, and lived experience, she explores how the everyday choices we make in our kitchens can become acts of environmental and social change. Her work has been featured on NPR, PBS, KTLA, CBS, KCRWs Good Food, and in the Los Angeles Times. She is the founder and Executive Director of the Pesticide Free Soil Project and the recipient of the Environmental Hero Award and the Gift of Freedom Award in Creative Nonfiction. Married and the mother of three Kitchen Activists, she splits her time between Oxnard, California, and Santa Fe, New Mexico.

All demos take place in the Foodwise Classroom (green tent in front of the Ferry Building) and are free to the public, with recipes and samples for all.

The demo will be followed by a book signing with book sales courtesy of Book Passage

events.description:
Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing.

Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu.

Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. events.description:
Ever since Rock & Roll and Blues Hall Of Famer Elvin Bishop first hit the scene with the Paul Butterfield Blues Band back in 1965, he's blazed his own musical trail. Whether he was playing raw, eye-popping blues, or penning the evergreen radio hit Fooled Around And Fell In Love, or touring the world for decades delivering his original, good-time countrified blues, Bishop has always inspired his fans with his rowdy guitar playing and witty, slice-of-life songs. Rolling Stone calls Bishop "a legendary guitarist" whose playing is "impeccable and spirited...a distinguished American player."

Late in 2015, Elvin Bishop formed The Big Fun Trio, with Bishop on guitar and vocals, and his friends Bob Welsh on piano and guitar and Willy Jordan on cajón (a hand-played Peruvian drumbox) and vocals. After playing just a handful of live dates, the group's instantly crowd-pleasing music and undeniable chemistry took the blues world by storm. With the release of their self-titled CD in 2017, media and fan response was immediate and overwhelming. DownBeat celebrated Bishop's "verbal hijinks, outstanding guitar work and country boy friendliness." OffBeat said The Big Fun Trio was "intricate, funky and uplifting," declaring them, "consistently great." With its top-shelf musicianship and front-porch vibe, the album earned a Grammy Award nomination.

events.title: Spotlight Sundays: The Enduring Spirit of Japanese Performing Arts
events.description:
Join koto artist and cultural historian Shirley Kazuyo Muramoto and her son, Brian Mitsuhiro Wong, for an engaging program exploring the resilience of Japanese traditional performing arts during World War II incarceration. Through live performances, personal stories, and a presentation of instruments and other personal objects preserved from the camps, they will illuminate how Japanese American artists sustained their cultural traditions under extreme circumstances.

The program will open with a traditional Japanese performance with Shirley and Brian, followed by a screening of Hidden Legacy: Japanese Traditional Performing Arts in the World War II Internment Camps, and a panel discussion moderated by Dr. Kirk Kanesaka, a kabuki actor, Japanese classical dancer, and assistant professor of Japanese and Asian Studies at California State University. Visitors are then invited to explore these historic objects and try their hand at playing a traditional Japanese instrument.

This program is a part of our exhibition programming for BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration on view through December 27, 2026.

Oakland Museum of California (OMCA) is committed to providing programs that are accessible, welcoming, and inclusive of our community. Wheelchairs, sensory inclusive devices, and additional amenities are available for checkout on a first come, first served basis at the Ticketing Desk. From Academy Award–winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR) comes a moving exploration of time, memory, and human connection.

Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs, whose life takes an unexpected turn when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), a Japanese playwright. As the two women reflect on the lives they’ve lived, they discover new ways to understand the time that remains. Attentive to the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a deeply humane film about the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and connection.

“GORGEOUS… the rarest type of film, not merely good enough to remind you what cinema can be, but great enough to remind you what life can be.” — Jessica Kiang, Variety

events.title: Bitter Christmas
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
A film by Pedro Almodóvar
Bitter Christmas
Monday, December 21 | The Castro

In Spanish with English subtitles

Join us at the historic Castro Theatre, for a festive holiday screening of Bitter Christmas, from acclaimed Spanish director and master of queer cinema, Pedro Almodóvar.

Bitter Christmas tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl’s alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can’t help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

Experience Almodovar’s trademark storytelling where it is meant to be seen – San Francisco’s premiere movie palace, The Castro Theatre!

events.title: Red Rocket
events.description:
Burnt out by the LA adult film scene, washed-up porn star Mikey Saber (Simon Rex) heads back to his old stomping grounds in small-town Texas. After a not-so-successful attempt at reconnecting with his estranged wife, Lexi (Bree Elrod), he forms an instant connection with Strawberry (Suzanna Son). Soon he’s juggling jealous exes, new love, and drug-dealing locals, all with a smile on his face. Who says you can’t go home again?

The audacious new film from writer-director Sean Baker (THE FLORIDA PROJECT, TANGERINE), starring Simon Rex in a magnetic, live-wire performance, RED ROCKET is a darkly funny and humane portrait of a uniquely American hustler and the hometown that barely tolerates him.

The San Jose Nutcracker takes place in San Jose at the turn of the last century. This unique production features landmarks of the era, with dazzling new scenic elements including a growing replica of the historic San Jose Light Tower and a skyline of San Jose inspired by the city in 1905. Costumes for the first act were inspired by period dolls from the History San Jose archives and the second act was inspired by our valley in the last century, carpeted in orchard blossoms and known as “The Valley of Heart’s Delight.” Swirling snowflakes, waltzing flowers, and The Sugarplum Fairy will make this holiday ballet a new favorite for the entire family!

Shelley Winters stars in Hammer Film's cult holiday hagsploitation classic Who Slew Auntie Roo? (1972) at the Great Star Theater on Tuesday, December 22 at 8pm. $25/21+

It's all part of DJ Dank's Movie Party along with "We Love Shelley Winters" trivia, prizes and a Holiday of Horrors drag show starring Ferosha Titties, Elsa Touche, Abortia Clinik and Brandelicious.

Director Curtis Harrington (Night Tide, Queen of Blood, Games, What's The Matter With Helen?, The Killing Kind) brings this choice slice of hagsploitation to life with Winters playing a reclusive actress who invites orphans to her home for Christmas as her touch on reality slips in this macabre take on the Hansel & Gretel fairytale with a script from legendary Hammer Films scribe Jimmy Sangster (Horror of Frankenstein, Dracula: Prince of Darkness, The Anniversary, The Nanny).

Also starring "Oliver" himself Mark Lester, Chloe Franks (The Uncanny), Lionel Jeffries (The Revenge of Frankenstein), Michael Gothard (The Devils) and Ralph Richardson (The Heiress, Fallen Idol).

Es un grupo diverso, donde el respeto es la base para que todos los asistentes puedan expresar libremente sus experiencias, identidad, étnicidad, nacionalidad, sexualidad, y creencias religiosas.

Todas las reuniones son en español y se llevan a cabo en un ambiente positivo, familiar, y confidencial. Ven a compartir con nosotros, estamos seguros que encontrarás apoyo y recibirás información para mejorar tu calidad de vida.

SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

Para mas información sobre El Grupo, llama al 415-632-9722.

_____

Our support group, El Grupo, has been a stable source of family and community for Latinos, Latinas and their families since the early 1980s. Join us for information about sexual health and harm reduction, meals and social support, and help finding health and social services.

Meetings are in-person at 940 Howard St Group Room A every Thursday from 3 to 5 pm.

QUEERSADA 2026: A Queer Posada
events.description:
A catered meal, chosen family vibes, and a place to kick it, all on Christmas Day.

For the fourth year, our annual FREE community meal returns!
It's a party, with catered food, movies on the screens, and chosen family vibes all afternoon.

We'll have pozole, pan con pavo, and more on the menu. The bar will be open (cash and credit card accepted) for any drinks you need. The food is on us, the drinks are on you.

How can you contribute? Bring a dessert you think people would like. Anything is a good thing!

And here's the thing: whether you celebrate the holiday or not isn't what we are concerned with.

The reality is, this can be a very challenging day for our community. Isolation, disconnection, hunger...

There is no reason we can't come together to make sure everybody has a safe, affirming place to go, and a good, dignified meal to eat, all in a familiar space.

And that's the thing: community is for everyone, regardless of age, income, professional or academic background, body type, and so on.

Questions? Follow us on IG and send us a DM: @boss.ideahouse

The event is free, but we are asking for each person coming to RSVP so we can keep an eye on the food and seating availability.

events.title: Dj Quik With Band
events.description: DJ Quik is a Compton, California, rapper and producer. When it comes to West Coast producers, DJ Quik is at the top of all lists. Classic albums such as Quik Is The Name (1990) and Way 2 Funky (1992) solidified DJ Quik in the ’90s Gangster Rap era of Hip Hop. Having put out several other albums since then, DJ Quik made his career producing for others. Known for his unique style of production, DJ Quik has been sought out by artists such as Jay-Z, Ludacris, Snoop Dogg, and many more to work on their projects. From a young age, Quik started to develop his musical prowess. At the age of 12, he was teaching himself how to play different instruments, and by the age of 21, he had become a multi-platinum-selling artist. After having released his first couple of albums, Quik launched his Mad Science Records label. Here, he would release Trauma (2005) and (2006), among many others that followed. Most recently, in 2016, DJ Quik put out the EP Rosecrans, a collaboration he did with Compton native rapper Problem.

events.title: Cinema Masala: Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge
events.description:
Audiences will fall in love with the charming Raj (Shah Rukh Khan) and the spirited Simran (Kajol), both Indians raised in the UK, who meet on a train when traveling with their friends across Europe. A frothy love story develops against picture-postcard Alpine landscapes, and the couple’s romance is threatened when Simran’s father takes her to India for an arranged marriage. The film wears its patriotism on its sleeve as it captures the conflict between modern attitudes toward love and traditional Indian values, where duty to the family takes precedence.

Three decades since its release, the magic of DILWALE DULHANIA LE JAYENGE (DDLJ) remains undiminished; the film still screens daily at the Maratha Mandir Theatre in Mumbai.

events.title: Vienna Teng
events.description:
Vienna Teng

Sunday, December 27 | The Freight

Some songs are the life of the party. Vienna Teng's are the back-porch conversation you still remember years later.

Her subversive choral piece "The Hymn of Acxiom” turns up in media literacy classes as well as drum corps shows (plus David Byrne’s blog, and the occasional flash mob choir in government buildings). The angst and effervescence in “Stray Italian Greyhound” has inspired anime music videos - and bridge-building political conversations.

Americana-tinged "City Hall" has quietly become a queer anthem, a soundtrack for coming-out journeys. The electro-pop exhortations of “Level Up” have powered many a doctoral dissertation, first novel, and courageous battle with illness. “Harbor” is a beloved first dance at weddings and a graduation gift. “Lullabye For A Stormy Night” has been woven into countless bedtime rituals. These are songs that not only age well, but remain trusted friends throughout people’s lives.

It helps that Vienna's sound has never stood still. Her warm, delicate mezzo has drawn listeners since 2002, when her debut Waking Hour landed appearances on NPR's Weekend Edition, The Late Show with David Letterman, and the top of Amazon’s charts. But she’s built different worlds around that voice from album to album: the string-laced intimacy of Warm Strangers, the hushed jazz of Dreaming Through the Noise, the eclectically ambitious Inland Territory, the shimmering electronica of Aims.

She’s world-built for othe...

events.title: Dj Quik With Band
events.description: DJ Quik is a Compton, California, rapper and producer. When it comes to West Coast producers, DJ Quik is at the top of all lists. Classic albums such as Quik Is The Name (1990) and Way 2 Funky (1992) solidified DJ Quik in the ’90s Gangster Rap era of Hip Hop. Having put out several other albums since then, DJ Quik made his career producing for others. Known for his unique style of production, DJ Quik has been sought out by artists such as Jay-Z, Ludacris, Snoop Dogg, and many more to work on their projects. From a young age, Quik started to develop his musical prowess. At the age of 12, he was teaching himself how to play different instruments, and by the age of 21, he had become a multi-platinum-selling artist. After having released his first couple of albums, Quik launched his Mad Science Records label. Here, he would release Trauma (2005) and (2006), among many others that followed. Most recently, in 2016, DJ Quik put out the EP Rosecrans, a collaboration he did with Compton native rapper Problem.

events.title: The Apartment
events.description:
A young upstart, C.C. Baxter (Jack Lemmon), will do anything to move up in the world...even loan out his apartment to the higher-ups for their romantic flings and extramarital trysts. All seems relatively fine and dandy until C.C. finds a romance of his own.

Billy Wilder is a genius – there aren't enough words in the world to describe all the films he's made and express how much he means to cinema – but in 1960, Wilder wrote and directed a perfect movie. I'm not saying this to sell you on the idea of seeing this film at the Alamo; I'm stating it as a fact. There are very few instances where you watch a movie and realize you are witnessing pure magnificence in that moment. Sometimes you think about a movie after the fact, and it gets better and better until you begin to love a movie you previously only really liked. THE APARTMENT is NOT one of those movies. It is a movie where, within 15 minutes of watching, you realize it is unlike anything you have ever seen before. Jack Lemmon is amazing, Shirley MacLaine is a full-on pixie dream girl, and the chemistry and dialogue snap and sparkle like you wouldn't believe.

events.title: Vienna Teng
events.description:
Vienna Teng

Monday, December 28 | The Freight

Some songs are the life of the party. Vienna Teng's are the back-porch conversation you still remember years later.

Her subversive choral piece "The Hymn of Acxiom” turns up in media literacy classes as well as drum corps shows (plus David Byrne’s blog, and the occasional flash mob choir in government buildings). The angst and effervescence in “Stray Italian Greyhound” has inspired anime music videos - and bridge-building political conversations.

Americana-tinged "City Hall" has quietly become a queer anthem, a soundtrack for coming-out journeys. The electro-pop exhortations of “Level Up” have powered many a doctoral dissertation, first novel, and courageous battle with illness. “Harbor” is a beloved first dance at weddings and a graduation gift. “Lullabye For A Stormy Night” has been woven into countless bedtime rituals. These are songs that not only age well, but remain trusted friends throughout people’s lives.

It helps that Vienna's sound has never stood still. Her warm, delicate mezzo has drawn listeners since 2002, when her debut Waking Hour landed appearances on NPR's Weekend Edition, The Late Show with David Letterman, and the top of Amazon’s charts. But she’s built different worlds around that voice from album to album: the string-laced intimacy of Warm Strangers, the hushed jazz of Dreaming Through the Noise, the eclectically ambitious Inland Territory, the shimmering electronica of Aims.

She’s world-built for othe...

events.title: The Shining
events.description:
An alcoholic, out-of-work teacher takes a job as the wintertime caretaker of a snowy resort. He brings his wife and young son with him. He wants to get some writing done. Things take a very dark turn...

THE SHINING is Stanley Kubrick’s chilling symphony of deft manipulation: Wendy Carlos’ score alternating with Ligeti compositions, Jack Nicholson and Shelley Duvall’s push-and-pull performances, and the omniscient Steadicam taking the whole thing in. THE SHINING transcends any trappings of paperback adaptation or genre exercise to become one of the most elementally terrifying works of art of the 20th century. Come lose yourself in its marvelous madness on the big screen, where it forever belongs.

events.title: When Harry Met Sally...
events.description:
We all know those couples. They see each other from across the room, they meet, and wham! They’re desperately in love.

That’s not the case for Harry and Sally. In fact, when they meet, they don’t particularly like each other. Sally is earnest and good. Harry is cynical and depressive. It’s not a match made in heaven.

But lovers of rom-coms know that opposites have a way of attracting.

With some of the most palpable on-screen chemistry in movie history, Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan take viewers on a journey through friendship, heartbreak, and the pitfalls of relationships with the help of expert direction from Rob Reiner, a pitch-perfect supporting cast (including Carrie Fisher and Bruno Kirby), and one of the best romantic comedy screenplays of all time from the brilliant Nora Ephron.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart - Symphony #41 in C Major, K. 551 “Jupiter”

When Mozart completed his final symphony in the summer of 1788, he created a work so vast in ambition and so perfect in execution that it earned the name of the greatest of the Roman gods, the Jupiter.

While Mozart’s star had already secured its place in the sky above, our program begins with two stars, still shooting upwards. Lili Boulanger’s D'un matin de printemps is a breath of fresh spring radiance followed by 14-year-old phenom, pianist Isabel Feng performing Mendelssohn’s dramatic and scintillating Concerto No1 in G minor.

events.title: El Grupo de Apoyo Latino
events.description:
El Grupo de Apoyo Latino de SFAF es un grupo social y educativo que ofrece un espacio abierto, seguro, y confidencial para apoyar a la comunidad Latina afectada por el VIH y SIDA. Es un grupo diverso, donde el respeto es la base para que todos los asistentes puedan expresar libremente sus experiencias, identidad, étnicidad, nacionalidad, sexualidad, y creencias religiosas.

Todas las reuniones son en español y se llevan a cabo en un ambiente positivo, familiar, y confidencial. Ven a compartir con nosotros, estamos seguros que encontrarás apoyo y recibirás información para mejorar tu calidad de vida.

SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

Para mas información sobre El Grupo, llama al 415-632-9722.

_____

Our support group, El Grupo, has been a stable source of family and community for Latinos, Latinas and their families since the early 1980s. Join us for information about sexual health and harm reduction, meals and social support, and help finding health and social services.

Meetings are in-person at 940 Howard St Group Room A every Thursday from 3 to 5 pm.

events.title: Mars Attacks!
events.description:
How do you follow the success of gargantuan blockbusters like BATMAN and BATMAN RETURNS? Well, if you’re oddball director Tim Burton, you decide to make a campy, violent, big-budget alien invasion comedy based on a series of sci-fi trading cards from the 1960s.

With an absurdly star-studded cast, including Pierce Brosnan, Glenn Close, Annette Bening, Danny DeVito, Michael J. Fox, Martin Short, Natalie Portman, Jack Black, Sarah Jessica Parker's head on a chihuahua’s body, and Jack Nicholson in two different roles, MARS ATTACKS! is a demented piece of retro-pop madness that represents Tim Burton at his very best. If you've never seen this epic, raucously funny cult classic, don't miss your chance to experience it on the big screen.

events.title: Welcome the New Year with Compassion, Connection, and Ease
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
Celebrate the arrival of 2027 with the beloved New Year team—Sylvia Boorstein (a founding Spirit Rock teacher), Brahmani Liebman (Kripalu yoga teacher, trainer, and mindful movement teacher), Barbara Bogatin (San Francisco Symphony cellist and mindfulness educator).
Together, we’ll explore teachings from Sylvia’s list of reflections from 50 years of practice and teaching entitled “This is What I Know,” including how being the principal beneficiary of our own goodwill, meeting each moment with compassion, and how cultivating a relaxed, expansive mind helps our hearts absorb life’s shocks and release tension. Anchored in the truth of impermanence and our profound interrelatedness, we will look ahead to the new year with resilience and tender care.
Our time will include heartfelt Dharma reflections, meditation periods, storytelling, guided mindful movement, and live cello music. Please join us in community for this comforting and uplifting annual gathering as we welcome the year ahead together!

events.title: New Year's Day Family Kayaking: Harbor Seals & an Aircraft Carrier
events.price_text: Per family: early bird (until Dec. 13) $80 single-income / $100 dual-income family (up to 2 kids), then $100 / $120; $10 per extra child. Plus $90 per kayak, paid to the kayak vendor. Free spots set aside for low-income families.
events.description:
Presented by Family Adventure Squad
New Year's Day Family Kayaking: Harbor Seals & an Aircraft Carrier
Friday, Jan. 1, 2027 | Near Encinal Boat Launch, Alameda
Start the new year on the water! Family Adventure Squad leads an easy family kayak paddle in Alameda's calm, protected harbor, all the way around the historic USS Hornet, a massive WWII aircraft carrier. Watch for harbor seals lounging on the docks, plus sea lions, pelicans and shorebirds. A guide from the kayak vendor paddles with the group.
No paddling experience needed: we stay inside the harbor for about 1.5 hours, and most families fit in one double kayak. Afterwards we drive a few minutes to a family-friendly spot with a big sand pit for lunch and play. Each kid shares a wish for 2027, then we pull surprise crackers with paper crowns and little toys inside.
11:15 a.m. to about 2:30 p.m. If it rains, we'll move it to Sunday, Jan. 3. We set aside free spots for low-income families. Registration required; spots are limited.
Details and booking: https://familyadventuresquad.org/adventures/p/alameda-family-kayaking

events.title: Megalopolis
events.description:
Like the famed empire that Francis Ford Coppola’s epic passion project is styled after, MEGALOPOLIS is a towering, monumental spectacle that most people will think about at least once a day. The City of New Rome is at a crossroads. At one end sits Cesar Catilina (Adam Driver), the idealistic artist striving for a utopian future, and at the other sits Mayor Franklin Cicero (Giancarlo Esposito), a powerful figure perpetuating greed, special interests, and partisan warfare. Their titanic struggle will shake the foundations of their city and lay the groundwork for a new tomorrow.

As engrossing and ambitious as you would expect from the filmmaker behind THE GODFATHER and APOCALYPSE NOW, MEGALOPOLIS is an unforgettable vision that could only have come from Coppola. Of course, he didn’t do it alone, and everyone in the unbelievable cast (including Driver, Esposito, Nathalie Emmanuel, Aubrey Plaza, Laurence Fishburne, and more) delivers some of the most memorable performances of their careers.

events.title: Lord Huron
events.description:
Lord Huron was created by Los Angeles-based artist Ben Schneider in 2010. After writing and recording two independent EPs (Into the Sun and Mighty) on his own, demand grew for Lord Huron to perform live. Schneider recruited friends Mark Barry (percussion), Miguel Briseño (bass) and Tom Renaud (guitar). Having first played music together at the tender age of 12, the group reunited and quickly hit their stride, transforming the project into a full-fledged live band.

Lord Huron’s debut LP Lonesome Dreams was released in 2012 followed by Strange Trails in 2015. The latter featured the multi-platinum single “The Night We Met,” which has gone on to become one of Spotify’s Top 40 most-streamed songs of all time. In 2018, Lord Huron earned widespread critical acclaim and a Top 5 debut on the Billboard Top 200 with their third album, Vide Noir– while their following LP Long Lost garnered praise from NPR, Time, Los Angeles Times, Spin and Stereogum and sparked performances on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Jimmy Kimmel Live!, The Late Late Show with James Corden and CBS This Morning: Saturday. Their latest album The Cosmic Selector Vol. 1 was released in 2025 and brought the band’s live show into their largest venues to date, including Madison Square Garden in NYC and the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.

events.title: Lord Huron
events.description:
Lord Huron was created by Los Angeles-based artist Ben Schneider in 2010. After writing and recording two independent EPs (Into the Sun and Mighty) on his own, demand grew for Lord Huron to perform live. Schneider recruited friends Mark Barry (percussion), Miguel Briseño (bass) and Tom Renaud (guitar). Having first played music together at the tender age of 12, the group reunited and quickly hit their stride, transforming the project into a full-fledged live band.

Lord Huron’s debut LP Lonesome Dreams was released in 2012 followed by Strange Trails in 2015. The latter featured the multi-platinum single “The Night We Met,” which has gone on to become one of Spotify’s Top 40 most-streamed songs of all time. In 2018, Lord Huron earned widespread critical acclaim and a Top 5 debut on the Billboard Top 200 with their third album, Vide Noir– while their following LP Long Lost garnered praise from NPR, Time, Los Angeles Times, Spin and Stereogum and sparked performances on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Jimmy Kimmel Live!, The Late Late Show with James Corden and CBS This Morning: Saturday. Their latest album The Cosmic Selector Vol. 1 was released in 2025 and brought the band’s live show into their largest venues to date, including Madison Square Garden in NYC and the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.

From the great Frank Borzage comes this dreamy Depression-era fable, starring Spencer Tracy and a supernal Loretta Young.

Trina, a young woman without a home, meets the handsome, sharply-dressed Bill in a public park. After treating her to an expensive meal that he cannot pay for, Trina realizes that he too is down on his luck. The two decide to share Bill’s derelict home, paving the way for a budding romance surrounded by the colorful friends and neighbors of Hoover Flats. A showgirl, pregnancy, and Bill’s wandering tendencies are sure to test the strength of their relationship.

Kick off the new year with the ultimate cinematic journey. On Friday, January 8, 2027, Stanley Kubrick’s masterwork 2001: A Space Odyssey returns to the historic The Castro Theatre for an exclusive, large-format screening presented in glorious 70mm.

An imposing black structure provides a connection between the past and the future in this enigmatic adaptation of a short story by revered sci-fi author Arthur C. Clarke. When Dr. Dave Bowman (Keir Dullea) and other astronauts are sent on a mysterious mission, their ship’s computer system, HAL, begins to display increasingly strange behavior, leading up to a tense showdown between man and machine that results in a mind-bending trek through space and time.

With its themes of humanity vs. machinery, 2001: A Space Odyssey serves as a timelier-than-ever cautionary tale about the human race’s never-ending thirst for technological advancement. Don’t miss your chance to see this sci-fi classic on the Castro screen!

events.title: Deep Rest: Spiritual, Emotional, and Cellular Rejuvenation
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Elissa Epel, PhD and Nichol Joy Chase
Deep rest is a powerful pathway to healing, inviting ease, clarity, and equanimity. In this program, we explore the science and art of restoration—how meditation, breathwork, sensory immersion, restorative yoga, and live contemplative music nourish emotional and cellular renewal.
We also explore creativity and imagination as catalysts for transformation. Art forms like poetry, music, dance, and other creative expressions help soften stress patterns, expand perception, and open us to new ways of thinking and being.
Through these practices, a spacious, receptive quality of awareness becomes a bridge—from self to systems, from tension toward wholeness—as we rest in a supportive environment and beautiful setting, held by community and the earth itself.
Together, we reconnect with deep rest as a generative force, opening us to mystery, creativity, and the joyful possibilities of becoming.

events.address: 417 Alvarado Street, Monterey, CA, Monterey, CA, 93940
events.description: Margaret LeAnn Rimes Cibrian (born August 28, 1982) is an American singer, songwriter, actress and author. Rimes rose to stardom at age 13 following the release of her version of the Bill Mack song "Blue", becoming the youngest country music star since Tanya Tucker in 1972. Rimes made her breakthrough into country music in 1996 with her debut album, Blue, which reached No. 1 on the Top Country Albums chart and was certified multi-platinum in sales by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). The album's eponymous leadoff single, "Blue", became a Top 10 hit and Rimes gained national acclaim for her similarity to Patsy Cline's vocal style. When she released her second studio album in 1997, You Light Up My Life: Inspirational Songs, she moved towards country pop material, which set the trend for a string of albums released into the next decade.

events.title: The Dharma of Money: Transforming Your Relationship to Money
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
With Sherman Spencer, MBA
Who would you be if you had a new way of relating to money? We may meet the breath, the body, even our relationships with curious, non-judgmental attention—but when it comes to money, many of us check-out, feel shame, or continue anchoring to beliefs unknowingly. This program brings money into the light of awareness, weaving neuroscience, Buddhist psychology, the Four Noble Truths, and the four higher emotions to cultivate insight and prosperity.
Whatever your financial reality—struggling, stable, or thriving—you’ll find a spacious, judgment-free container to create a new future. The complexity of money presents surprising opportunities for transformation. You’ll learn how to uncover your wisdom, make decisions, mitigate the comparing mind, discover a way of relating to money that honors the current version of yourself, and cultivate a mindset conducive to financial wellness.
Together, we will decrease doubt, increase clarity, and create a life where money becomes your ally.
