events.title: CAKE
events.description:
Two Nights!

United for Ukraine

Another Planet Entertainment Presents
An Evening of Music, Remembrance & Solidarity
CAKE
Tuesday, January 12 | ​Fox Theater

CAKE is the Sacramento, California–based band that has built a singular body of work through an unwavering commitment to originality, independence, and creative self-determination.

Formed in the early 1990s as a somewhat antagonistic response to the prevailing grunge movement, CAKE developed its own democratic process and fiercely self-reliant approach—principles that have grown stronger over the decades. The result is a band that operates as its own musical nation-state, with few evident peers in sound and perspective.

CAKE writes, arranges, produces, records, and performs its music from its Sacramento-based, solar-powered studio, which regularly generates more electricity than the building consumes—enough to send the meter running backward. That same spirit of independence extends to every aspect of the band’s work, from its music and recordings to the way it approaches touring and its relationship with its audience.

The band’s most recent album, Showroom of Compassion, debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and was described by The New Yorker as “deadpan brilliance.” Across its catalog, CAKE seamlessly incorporates elements of rock, funk, country, jazz, soul, and Latin music without settling into any one genre. The result is a sound and vision unmistakably its own.

The original Broadway sensation returns to the road! Celebrating 20 years-Jersey style!

CAKE is the Sacramento, California–based band that has built a singular body of work through an unwavering commitment to originality, independence, and creative self-determination.

Formed in the early 1990s as a somewhat antagonistic response to the prevailing grunge movement, CAKE developed its own democratic process and fiercely self-reliant approach—principles that have grown stronger over the decades. The result is a band that operates as its own musical nation-state, with few evident peers in sound and perspective.

CAKE writes, arranges, produces, records, and performs its music from its Sacramento-based, solar-powered studio, which regularly generates more electricity than the building consumes—enough to send the meter running backward. That same spirit of independence extends to every aspect of the band’s work, from its music and recordings to the way it approaches touring and its relationship with its audience.

The band’s most recent album, Showroom of Compassion, debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and was described by The New Yorker as “deadpan brilliance.” Across its catalog, CAKE seamlessly incorporates elements of rock, funk, country, jazz, soul, and Latin music without settling into any one genre. The result is a sound and vision unmistakably its own.

events.title: Pepper
events.description:
Pepper
Friday, January 15 | ​The UC Theatre

"Kona Dub-Rock." That's how Pepper describes their blend of reggae, alternative rock, dub, island rhythms, and punk rock energy. It's a sound that's taken the trio from the Big Island of Hawaii — where vocalist/guitarist Kaleo Wassman, vocalist/bassist Bret Bollinger, and drummer Yesod Williams held their first band practice as teenagers in the late 1990s — to the upper reaches of Billboard's Reggae Albums chart, where 2019's Local Motion peaked at Number 1.

Nearly 25 years into the band's career, Pepper's three members are no longer merely artists. They're ambassadors to a thriving scene. As co-founders of their own record label, LAW Records, they've enriched the reggae community worldwide by reissuing albums by Steel Pulse and Jimmy Cliﬀ and releasing more than 20 other artists. As road warriors, they've traveled North America with The Wailers, 311, Pennywise, and Snoop Dogg, building a diverse community of collaborators and fans by blurring the boundaries that normally exist between genres. For Pepper, each new album is an opportunity not only to pay homage to their own reggae-rock roots, but also to expand the circle of connection, camaraderie, and synergy that surrounds the band.

events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment Presents
Winter Tour 2027
Greensky Bluegrass
Saturday, January 16 | Fox Theater

For two decades now, Greensky Bluegrass have been building an empire, brick by brick. They are widely known for their dazzling live performances and relentless touring schedule, but that is only the tip of the complex tale of the five musicians that make up Greensky Bluegrass: Anders Beck [dobro], Michael Arlen Bont [banjo], Dave Bruzza [guitar], Mike Devol [upright bass], and Paul Hoffman [Mandolin]. The five are connected through a deep bond, just as they are seasoned road warriors, they’re a band of brothers who have seen each other through decades of ups and downs, personal and collective highlights, and the moments when life turns it all upside down. These are real people having real experiences. As with traditional bluegrass, they write about their own contemporary day-to-day happenings, emotions, and experiences in the modern world.

The band’s underground die-hard fans pack out venues across the country. They travel in droves and sell out multiple-night show runs at iconic venues like Red Rocks and The Ryman.

“As songwriters and musicians, we have a need for people to be on board, we’re not just regurgitating the same shit,” explains Bruzza.

events.description:
Grammy®-nominated powerhouse singer-songwriter Beth Hart’s released a digital deluxe edition of her studio album, You Still Got Me, this year by Provogue / Mascot Label Group. The album features appearances by Eric Gales and Guns ‘n Roses’ Slash.

You Still Got Me is Hart’s eleventh studio album, and it finds her riding a career trajectory that has been heading for the stars for several years and keeps soaring. Her most recent albums, A Tribute to Led Zeppelin (2022) and War In My Mind (2019), became her highest charting UK and US releases to date, along with crashing into the Top 10 in Germany, France, Sweden, Belgium, Switzerland, Poland, Austria, and The Netherlands. Selling out shows worldwide, her recent travels have taken her across the US, Canada, Europe, and all the way to India, Morocco, and Australia.

events.title: Peter Rowan: Walls of Time
events.description:
Join Grammy Award-winning singer-songwriter and Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame inductee Peter Rowan for a special evening at the Freight celebrating the release of his new memoir, Walls of Time: Tales of a Bluegrass Pilgrim.

Part concert, part storytelling, and official Bay Area book launch, the evening will bring together the songs, stories, and extraordinary musical journey behind Walls of Time.

From joining Bill Monroe’s legendary Blue Grass Boys in 1965 to the San Francisco psychedelic scene and Old & In the Way with Jerry Garcia and David Grisman, Rowan has spent more than five decades at the crossroads of bluegrass tradition and musical reinvention.

Now, for the first time, Rowan tells that story in his own words. Walls of Time is a deeply personal journey through American roots music, legendary collaborations, spiritual searching, and a life devoted to following the music wherever it leads.

Celebrate the publication of Walls of Time in Berkeley—one of the places at the heart of Peter Rowan’s musical story.

The evening will feature live music, stories from the memoir, and a celebration of the release of Walls of Time. Books will be available at the show.

events.description:
Get your tickets here: Scents and Sensibility: On Fragrance and Scene-Craft with Athénaïs Nin

Join consummate lover of fragrance Athénaïs Nin for a lush, opulent, and indulgent exploration of the sensorium of scent and the many ways it can be incorporated into scene-craft and the evocation of mood, memory, energy, and emotion.

Some topics we’ll cover:
• A basic introduction to the science, craft, and character of fragrance;
• Scent and “involuntary memory” (Proust);
• Memory, trauma, and inciting “traumatisms” (Saketopoulou);
• Scent and evocations of mood or “kernel kinks” (Princess Kali); and
• Scent and fragrance as a tool for storytelling, and scene-craft
Come prepared to encounter a wide range of notes and fragrances—and through that active encounter, to engage with the scents to tell stories and island yourself in a sea of memory and desire.

events.title: John McCutcheon
events.description:
The Washington Post described John as folk music's "Rustic Renaissance Man," a moniker flawed only by its understatement. "Calling John McCutcheon a 'folksinger' is like saying Deion Sanders is just a football player..." (Dallas Morning News). Besides his usual circuit of major concert halls and theaters, John is equally at home in an elementary school auditorium, a festival stage o a farm rally. He is a whirlwind of energy packing five lifetimes into one.

In the past few years alone he has headlined over a dozen different festivals in North America (including repeated performances at the National Storytelling Festival), recorded an original composition for Virginia Public Television involving over 500 musicians, toured Australia for the sixth time, toured Chile in support of a women's health initiative, appeared in a Woody Guthrie tribute concert in New York City, gave a featured concert at the Smithsonian Folklife Festival, taught performance art skills at a North Carolina college, given symphony pops concerts across America, served as President of the fastest-growing Local in the Musicians Union and performed a special concert at the National Baseball Hall of Fame. This is all in his "spare time." His "real job," he's quick to point out, is father to two grown sons.

But it is in live performance that John feels most at home. It is what has brought his music into the lives and homes of one of the broadest audiences any folk musician has ever enjoyed.

Tape B, born Kemal Berk Alkanat, is a dynamic force in today’s electronic music scene, merging the nostalgic vibes of old-school dubstep with contemporary bass music and hip-hop. Born in Turkey and raised in the U.S. from the age of three, Tape B brings a distinctive sound that captivates with a blend of nostalgia and modernity, termed “Old School x New School.”

His musical journey began at the University of Central Florida, influenced by early 2000s hip-hop and electronic pioneers like UKF and The Glitch Mob. His career took a professional turn after a revelatory experience at the Lost Lands Music Festival in 2019. Tape B’s rise to prominence was fueled by viral SoundCloud mixes and dynamic live performances, including his iconic “Yo, Tape B” tag which has become a recognizable call throughout modern clubland and festivals.

Over the past year, Tape B has reached new heights, including a sold-out headline debut at Red Rocks Amphitheatre and a 33-date fall bus tour with standout sellouts at premier venues such as The Salt Shed, The Armory, Echostage, and The Shrine. His high-profile B3B performance alongside Zeds Dead and Subtronics to close out the year further solidified his place at the forefront of modern bass music, alongside a growing catalog of collaborations including work with GRiZ.

With continued support from industry leaders like Subtronics, Zeds Dead, Excision, Ganja White Night, Wooli, and Peekaboo, Tape B’s rise reflects both a deep respect for the roots of du...

events.title: The Legend of Korra in Concert - Broadway San Jose
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.description:
From the creators of the global hit Avatar: The Last Airbender in Concert comes the next chapter – The Legend of Korra in Concert. Celebrate 15 years of The Legend of Korra with a breathtaking live concert experience that brings the groundbreaking sequel to life through a live symphonic performance paired with an immersive cinematic experience. Follow Korra, a rebellious girl from the Southern Water Tribe and the next Avatar after Aang, as she steps into her role as the Avatar in a world on the brink of revolution. In Republic City, she clashes with powerful enemies, faces rising unrest, and is tested in ways that will define her legacy. Alongside her friends Asami, Bolin, Mako and Tenzin, Korra’s journey delivers one of the most thrilling and emotionally charged chapters in the Avatar saga. Across a two-hour visual journey through all four seasons of the iconic animated series, projected on a full-size cinema screen, audiences will experience the original dialogue and sound effects intact while a powerful live orchestra performs the legendary score in perfect sync with the action on screen. All brought together by the music of Emmy® Award winning composer Jeremy Zuckerman and original series editor Jeff Adams, The Legend of Korra in Concert is an unforgettable way to experience one of the most beloved animated worlds of all time.

events.title: Pictures At An Exhibition
events.description:
We invite you into our living art gallery where bold colors, sharp contrasts, and unforgettable images come together in a concert that celebrates artistry in all its forms.

Michael Daugherty’s American Gothic is a vibrant, witty homage to iconic American art and culture. Inspired by Grant Wood’s famous painting, Daugherty’s score blends driving rhythms, jazzy inflections, and unmistakably American energy into a work that is both playful and poignant.

The legendary Jon Nakamatsu returns center stage with Maurice Ravel’s Piano Concerto in G, a dazzling showcase of elegance and bite. Written in the spirit of jazz-age Paris, the concerto sparkles with bluesy harmonies, razor-sharp rhythms, and haunting lyricism.

Modest Mussorgsky’s monumental Pictures at an Exhibition is a sonic gallery tour inspired by paintings and drawings of the composer’s friend Viktor Hartmann. From the swaggering “Promenade” to the thunderous grandeur of “The Great Gate of Kiev,” Mussorgsky’s vivid musical portraits bring visual art to life in sweeping, unforgettable sound.

events.title: Pictures At An Exhibition
events.description:
We invite you into our living art gallery where bold colors, sharp contrasts, and unforgettable images come together in a concert that celebrates artistry in all its forms.

Michael Daugherty’s American Gothic is a vibrant, witty homage to iconic American art and culture. Inspired by Grant Wood’s famous painting, Daugherty’s score blends driving rhythms, jazzy inflections, and unmistakably American energy into a work that is both playful and poignant.

The legendary Jon Nakamatsu returns center stage with Maurice Ravel’s Piano Concerto in G, a dazzling showcase of elegance and bite. Written in the spirit of jazz-age Paris, the concerto sparkles with bluesy harmonies, razor-sharp rhythms, and haunting lyricism.

Modest Mussorgsky’s monumental Pictures at an Exhibition is a sonic gallery tour inspired by paintings and drawings of the composer’s friend Viktor Hartmann. From the swaggering “Promenade” to the thunderous grandeur of “The Great Gate of Kiev,” Mussorgsky’s vivid musical portraits bring visual art to life in sweeping, unforgettable sound.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: John Roseboro
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

John Roseboro

Known for his buttery voice and distinct strumming, guitarist, singer-songwriter and bandleader John Roseboro has been making a name for himself in the Brooklyn indie scene, redefining and innovating the genre with Brazilian jazz and mysticism.

Building off of the likes of João Gilberto and Antônio Carlos Jobim, Roseboro’s post-bossa style carries other similarities to the greats in that his music focuses on personal and social justice, undertaking major themes such as human rights, love, and religion, being described as "probably the music that will heal the world... impossible to be indifferent, in voice and soul.”

John cites his upbringing, particularly living with the Amish and years as a mortician, as informing his playing and perspective. The new artist has received praise from indie giants Men I Trust, Frankie Cosmos, Field Medic, Thee Sacred Souls, drawing comparisons to King Krule, Steve Lacy, Burt Bacharach, and Elliott Smith.

On Thursday, November 19, Heather Knight, San Francisco bureau chief for The New York Times, will moderate a panel featuring Will Hearst, editor and publisher of Alta Journal; award-winning television journalist Wendy Tokuda; political reporter Joe Fitzgerald Rodriguez of The San Francisco Standard; and radio host and political commentator John F. Rothmann.

From newspaper dispatches to television broadcasts, radio conversations and news delivered through smartphones, San Francisco’s media have chronicled a city defined by reinvention. Earthquakes, local politics, cultural movements, housing challenges and unforgettable personalities have provided generations of journalists with stories that resonate far beyond the Bay Area.
Bringing together perspectives from print, television, digital news and radio, the evening will explore how the city’s stories reach audiences, how journalism has changed and what endures as new technologies reshape the media landscape. Guests will hear from people who have brought Bay Area news into homes, onto doorsteps, over the airwaves and into the palm of a hand.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

with Filmmaker Emiko Omori and
Satsuki Ina, author of The Poet and the Silk Girl
About the Film from the Defiant to the Last website:
“Based on lies and wartime propaganda, during WWII the U.S. government forcibly removed and incarcerated more than 125,000 innocent Japanese Americans in ten American concentration camps, solely because of their race.
“At all the prison sites, despite the mythology of quiet compliance, Japanese Americans showed moral courage, resisted, and refused to accept the government’s abuse. Defiant to the Last tells the story of the Tule Lake Segregation Center where dissident Japanese Americans were demonized and punished for speaking out against the false wartime incarceration.”
Revolution Books is showing this film because the story of resistance to the unjust treatment of the Japanese Americans in WW II resonates deeply with our own time, when immigrants’ rights are stripped away, they are demonized, and some deported to torture prisons in countries they’ve never lived in – and people who oppose this treatment are attacked and vilified by the government.
This is a time for defiance, for voices of conscience to speak out, and for revolution. Defiant to the Last brings crucial experience and important lessons from the past, and we are very glad to be able to bring Satsuki Ina and Emiko Omori to our store.

events.description:
Jordan Joel

Jordan Joel presents the debut of their newest collection

Trash Prom Walk of Shame
Trash Prom turns shame into spectacle: alchemy, excess and reclamation, built from what the world throws away. The Walk of Shame becomes a walk of pride, a celebration of personal survival in scraps and iridescence.

Here, the discarded is sacred. Trash couture walks alongside upcycled pieces and ready-to-wear, each look in conversation with the others. Together they carry a confession: the things we were told to hide, stitched back together and sent down the runway in full camp glory.
Shame isn’t erased. It’s raw material, and transgression is how it transforms.
Beyond fashion, the night becomes an immersive world of performance art, interactive installations, music and a live atelier.
Join the inaugural Queer Heartstrings, the first iteration of a collective textile creation, and watch transformation happen up close as you become part of the show.
Come as you are, as you were, or as who you’re becoming.
Walk in carrying whatever you’ve been holding, and walk out shining.

Pi.1415926535
The free PresidiGo Shuttle system welcomes park visitors, residents, and employees with fully accessible shuttles and bike racks.
There are two PresidiGo Shuttle services, each with different policies and guidelines – Around the Park and Downtown.

Downtown (Free on Weekends)
The Downtown express route make stops at the Presidio Transit Center on the Main Post, the Letterman District, Union Street/Van Ness Avenue, Embarcadero BART, and the Transbay Terminal.
The shuttle operates from 5:45 am to 9:30 pm on weekdays and 10 am to 7:30 pm on weekends. On weekdays, during the evening commute (leaving the Presidio only) from 4-7:40 pm, a valid MUNI Passport (not a MUNI Fast Pass) is required. No pass is required on weekends.
It’s free for Presidio Employees and Residents every day with an appropriate boarding pass. Connecting service to Caltrain is available.
The Downtown PresidiGo does not operate on federal holidays.
Around the Park (Every Day – 2 Routes)
Around the Park is free and available to visitors, residents, and employees all day. The shuttle runs two continuous 30-minute loops:

The Crissy Field Route serves the northern Presidio including the Main Post, Golden Gate Bridge, Fort Scott and Letterman District

The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

Join Bay Area–raised, Los Angeles–based contemporary artist Amadour for a free, all-ages art workshop in San Francisco exploring geometric abstraction, Land Art, and the landscapes of the American West. This hands-on family workshop invites visitors of all ages to discover the connections between contemporary art, nature, and creative expression.
Through a lively art history presentation, participants will learn about the work of influential artists of the American West, including Agnes Martin, Nancy Holt, and Michael Heizer, exploring how artists have transformed landscapes through geometry, abstraction, and large-scale interventions in nature.
Following the presentation, participants will experiment with line, shape, color, and space through interactive activities and hands-on yarn art-making, creating their own abstract landscapes to take home.

Amadour is an artist, writer, and musician raised in Reno, Nevada, and Sausalito, California, with Mexican and Colombian roots. Their interdisciplinary practice explores geometric abstraction, architecture, landscape, and the cultural histories of the American West.

events.description:
Studio MGHJack Scott: Large-Scale Drawings
Monumental charcoal drawings unseen for forty years return to College of Marin, where the artist began November 16 to December 11, 2026 · Opening reception Saturday, November 21, 3 to 5 pm · College of Marin Fine Arts Gallery, Kentfield, CA
KENTFIELD, CA · Studio MGH and College of Marin present Jack Scott: Large-Scale Drawings, the first public exhibition in forty years of the monumental charcoal drawings Jack Scott made in the 1970s and 1980s. Worked on unstretched unprimed canvas, some reaching 22 feet, each drawing is built from a single repeated mark. Scott developed his own fixative, and four decades later the surfaces remain immaculate. In his time, Scott was one of the most closely watched artists in California. He had solo exhibitions at the Los Angeles Institute of Contemporary Art, Hansen Fuller Goldeen Gallery in San Francisco, and Kirk deGooyer Gallery in Los Angeles. He received a National Endowment for the Arts Artist Fellowship in drawing (1981), was three times a finalist for SFMOMA’s SECA Award (1980, 1981, 1988), and was twice nominated for the Oakland Museum’s Annual Art Award. His work was reviewed in Artforum, the San Francisco Chronicle, the Los Angeles Times, Artweek, and by Rebecca Solnit in the Pacific Sun, and is included in Thomas Albright’s Art in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1945–1980. Robert McDonald wrote in Artweek: “His works must be seen.” Then the drawings, too large and too physical to place easily...

events.title: Opening Reception: Me, Nature, As One
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPhoto of artworks courtesy of the artists.Join Qualia Contemporary Art on Saturday, November 21, 2026, for the opening reception of Me, Nature, As One.
Me, Nature, As One is a group exhibition spanning multiple generations whose work traces the evolution and reimagining of shanshui, the classical tradition of landscape painting. Across ink, watercolor, photography, mixed media, and calligraphy, the exhibition presents work that imbues nature with spirituality, internal landscapes, and existential philosophy.

Shanshui, literally “mountain and water,” has never been about depicting nature alone. For centuries, it has sought nature’s spiritual essence and asked a broader question about humanity’s place within it. The featured artists—Victoria Yau, Zhang Yu, Stella Zhang, Meng Huang, Xu Hongming, Jiang Heng, and Chu Chu—reinterpret this classical form while keeping that inquiry alive, guided by the idea that self and nature are not separate but shape one another through subjective experience.

The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.title: Incredible Sugar Castle At The Westin St. Francis
events.description:
The Westin St. FrancisA San Francisco holiday tradition turns 21 this year! Executive Pastry Chef Jean-François Houdré and his team proudly unveil the nearly 12-foot-tall Sugar Castle, a dazzling, handcrafted replica of a French château that has delighted visitors since 2005.
This beloved holiday masterpiece weighs more than 1,000 pounds and features more than 20 towers, approximately 15 illuminated rooms, and a working train, bringing a whimsical French château to life in the heart of Union Square.
New This Year: “Can You Find San Francisco?”
Get ready for a San Francisco treasure hunt! Hidden throughout the Sugar Castle is a replica of the hotel’s beloved dog mascot, Francis, as well as miniature versions of some of the city’s most iconic landmarks, brought to life with custom-designed ornaments generously donated by San Francisco Mercantile. From the Golden Gate Bridge to a classic cable car, guests can find them all, collect the letters, and unscramble the secret word to claim a prize. It’s a playful way for visitors of all ages to discover a little more of San Francisco tucked inside the castle.

Sugar Castle Puzzles
The magic of the Sugar Castle can live on long after the holidays. A one-of-a-kind, custom-made Sugar Castle puzzle captures the intricate details of this beloved San Francisco tradition, inviting visitors to recreate the spectacular confectionery masterpiece piece by piece at home. Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

SF’s 2026 Union Square’s Great Holiday Tree (Nov. 27 – Jan. 1)
Macy's
For generations, Union Square’s iconic Christmas tree has been a centerpiece of San Francisco’s holiday season, drawing visitors downtown to see the city sparkle for the holidays. But 2026 brings a big change to this beloved tradition: after years of towering artificial trees, Union Square is welcoming a real, 60-foot white fir for the first time since 2010.
2026 update: The live tree arrived in Union Square on November 19 and is scheduled to be lit on Friday, November 27, 2026 (the day after Thanksgiving).
The tree was grown in Burney, in Shasta County, and traveled to San Francisco to become the centerpiece of the city’s holiday celebrations. It’s a major change from the previous Macy’s-sponsored artificial tree, which stood more than 83 feet tall and featured 43,000 LED lights and 700 ornaments.

Macy’s is no longer sponsoring the tree, but the holiday tradition lives on. The Union Square Alliance and the city are stepping in to keep a festive centerpiece in the plaza, with the tree lighting up the square throughout the holiday season.
Stop by Union Square Plaza to see San Francisco’s newest Christmas tree, just across the street from the Macy’s flagship store. The tree is scheduled to remain illuminated through January 1, 2027.

events.title: SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

The Cow Palace, 2600 Geneva Avenue, Daly City, CA
Saturdays and Sundays, November 21 to December 20, 2026, plus Friday, November 27, the day after Thanksgiving, from 10 am to 6 pm

events.title: Santa’s Riverboat Arrival and Shop Small Saturday (Petaluma)
events.description:
Jim JohnsonWatch Santa and Mrs. Claus cruise into town on a Lind Marine tugboat Saturday, November 28, for photos and festivities. Arrive at 11:30 am with your family and friends to enjoy live entertainment from the Pacific Empire Chorus while waiting for Santa and Mrs. Claus to arrive! By noon, the couple will disembark at the Turning Basin. Young Nutcracker-costumed dancers from Petaluma School of Ballet will escort the couple to their special holiday tent adjacent to Taps on the River for photos with eager children. The jolly pair will leave at 1:30 pm for their next stop on their holiday tour.
November 28 is also Shop Small Saturday. As you queue up for photos, grab a Shop Small bag filled with items from local merchants, while supply lasts. Bring your holiday shopping lists and support local! Historic downtown, filled with boutiques from chic to quirky and fortifying farm-to-table dining and tasting rooms, is just a couple blocks away. The kids will love spotting Holiday Hen Hunt chickens in shop windows to fill their bingo cards for a chance to win prizes!
If you’re coming from out of town, the festivities are just three blocks from the Petaluma Downtown Smart Station, so you can skip the parking and the traffic, while doing a solid for the planet.

events.address: Geary and Powell, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
SF’s 2026 Union Square’s Great Holiday Tree (Nov. 27 – Jan. 1)
Macy's
For generations, Union Square’s iconic Christmas tree has been a centerpiece of San Francisco’s holiday season, drawing visitors downtown to see the city sparkle for the holidays. But 2026 brings a big change to this beloved tradition: after years of towering artificial trees, Union Square is welcoming a real, 60-foot white fir for the first time since 2010.
2026 update: The live tree arrived in Union Square on November 19 and is scheduled to be lit on Friday, November 27, 2026 (the day after Thanksgiving).
The tree was grown in Burney, in Shasta County, and traveled to San Francisco to become the centerpiece of the city’s holiday celebrations. It’s a major change from the previous Macy’s-sponsored artificial tree, which stood more than 83 feet tall and featured 43,000 LED lights and 700 ornaments.

Macy’s is no longer sponsoring the tree, but the holiday tradition lives on. The Union Square Alliance and the city are stepping in to keep a festive centerpiece in the plaza, with the tree lighting up the square throughout the holiday season.
Stop by Union Square Plaza to see San Francisco’s newest Christmas tree, just across the street from the Macy’s flagship store. The tree is scheduled to remain illuminated through January 1, 2027.

events.title: Indigenous Voices: Joey Clift and Terria Smith in conversation
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerTelHiLitJoin us as we close out our Native American Heritage Month series, welcoming Joey Clift and Terria Smith to share their latest works — We’ve Been Here The Whole Time! and I Love You So Many.
Free to attend — RSVP required to reserve your seat.

Speakers
Joey Clift is a Los Angeles-based, Peabody and 2x Emmy Award-nominated comedian, writer, director, producer and enrolled member of the Cowlitz Indian Tribe.
Joey attended college to become a local TV weather person because as a kid he didn’t see any Native American comedians on television, and that made him believe he wasn’t allowed to work in comedy. Since then he has learned that this is not true – and his comedy style reflects that. Joey’s work has been featured in The Washington Post, Pitchfork, NPR, Dead Meat, Dropout and Comedy Central.
Terria Smith is a tribal member of the Torres Martinez Desert Cahuilla Indians and a proud original Californian. She is the editor of News from Native California magazine and director of the Berkeley Roundhouse, Heyday’s California Indian publishing program. Smith is also the editor of the 2023 anthology Know We Are Here: Voices of Native California Resistance. She received her undergraduate degree at Cal Poly Humboldt (formerly Humboldt State University) and earned her master’s degree at the UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism. She lives on her ancestral homelands in the Coachella Valley with her puppy Havana.

events.description:
$5 Off Tix: San Francisco Playhouse’s “Peter Pan Goes Wrong” (Sept. 26-Nov. 28)
San Francisco Playhouse
By Henry Lewis, Henry Shields & Jonathan Sayer The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan. Save $5 off tickets with code FUNCHEAP.
It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

SF’s 2026 Union Square’s Great Holiday Tree (Nov. 27 – Jan. 1)
Macy's
For generations, Union Square’s iconic Christmas tree has been a centerpiece of San Francisco’s holiday season, drawing visitors downtown to see the city sparkle for the holidays. But 2026 brings a big change to this beloved tradition: after years of towering artificial trees, Union Square is welcoming a real, 60-foot white fir for the first time since 2010.
2026 update: The live tree arrived in Union Square on November 19 and is scheduled to be lit on Friday, November 27, 2026 (the day after Thanksgiving).
The tree was grown in Burney, in Shasta County, and traveled to San Francisco to become the centerpiece of the city’s holiday celebrations. It’s a major change from the previous Macy’s-sponsored artificial tree, which stood more than 83 feet tall and featured 43,000 LED lights and 700 ornaments.

Macy’s is no longer sponsoring the tree, but the holiday tradition lives on. The Union Square Alliance and the city are stepping in to keep a festive centerpiece in the plaza, with the tree lighting up the square throughout the holiday season.
Stop by Union Square Plaza to see San Francisco’s newest Christmas tree, just across the street from the Macy’s flagship store. The tree is scheduled to remain illuminated through January 1, 2027.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: $1.50 Admission Day for Ripley’s Believe It or Not!’s Final Day in SF
events.venue: Ripley’s Believe It or Not Odditorium
events.description:
Google MapsRipley’s Believe It or Not! is closing its San Francisco Odditorium at Fisherman’s Wharf on Dec. 1, 2026, ending nearly 60 years of strange sights at 175 Jefferson St. The attraction first opened on Feb. 2, 1967, and it’s sending things off with a suitably weird farewell.
On its final day, admission will cost just $1.50 for adults and 75 cents for kids, matching the original 1967 ticket prices. Want to visit before then? Ripley’s is also offering $19.67 admission on Thursdays during its final weeks.
The museum is auctioning off select exhibits and artifacts through a silent auction that stays open until closing. Among the oddities up for grabs are a Golden Gate Bridge made on the head of a pin, toothpick replicas of the bridge, Joe DiMaggio’s crutches, a chicken-wire portrait of Janis Joplin, a matchstick cable car and even a fur-covered fish. There’s also a 1989 Emmy tied to coverage of the Loma Prieta earthquake and World Series.

The building is already being marketed for lease, so the future of this longtime Wharf attraction remains up in the air.
H/t SF Chronicle

events.title: Meet Nina LaCour, Author of Meet Me in the Garden
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerNew Orleans, 1944. Odette has always been one of the Honore sisters, glamorous and admired in their Creole community. But while Odette’s older sisters are content to be wives and mothers, Odette has always wanted something else. It is only with her beloved cousin, Delphine, that Odette can tell her secret: she is in love with a woman, and she longs to be an artist. Delphine has a secret lover, too, a white man. In the hidden garden they’ve discovered, Odette and Delphine can dream of futures full of passion and freedom.
But five years later, Odette’s life is nothing like what she’d planned. She’s a widowed mother, living in Los Angeles, and she and Delphine, who is passing as white, have spiraled away from each other. When Delphine reaches a breaking point, Odette must make a shattering choice to try to hold her family together.

Profound and expansive, a story of love and longing, art and motherhood, friendship and desire, Meet Me in the Garden is a decades-spanning tour de force, inspired by the author’s family and tracing the history of the Great Migration.
Giveaway copies of Meet Me in the Garden will be available on a first-come first-serve basis at the event while supplies last.
Nina LaCour is the bestselling, Michael L. Printz Award and Lambda Literary Award-winning author of picture books, a chapter book series, young adult novels, and adult literary fiction. Her novel We Are Okay was named one of TIME Magazine’s Top 100 YA Novels of Al...

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: “Decoder” Film Screening: Analog-Age Anti-Capitalist Riot
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer© Interzone PicturesIn an early cyberpunk version of 1980s Berlin, audiophile F.M. (played by F.M. Einheit of the legendary German noise band Einstürzende Neubauten) spends his nights tuned into the peaceful, unobtrusive Muzak played from nearby H Burger restaurants. But when he discovers that it secretly carries subliminal messages encouraging mindless consumption, he teams up with a group of urban pirates (led by Genesis P-Orridge) to spread a musical antidote. Its patrons awakened from their fast-food slumber and on the edge of all-out anti-capitalist insurrection, H Burger headquarters decides to dispatch a special agent to permanently deal with their F.M. problem.
Inspired by a 1970 essay by William S. Burroughs (who also stars in the film) and featuring the music of Soft Cell, Einstürzende Neubauten, and The The, Decoder doubles as a midnight cult gem and an analog-age riot against the encroachment of technology on the autonomy of human desire and perception.

events.title: Artist Talk with Klea McKenna
events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerKlea McKennaJoin us on December 3rd at 6pm for an artist talk with 2025–26 Kala Fellow Klea McKenna. McKenna will share the process of making her installation The Remedy–both how she makes large shaped-plate intaglio prints using cardboard plates–as well as her writing and illustration process. In this work Klea began with the seed of a family story, passed down to her by her maternal line. Using writing and illustration exercises she grew it into a written short story and then a mixed media installation. Klea will share her methods for moving between memory, writing, research and visual imagery. The Remedy is on view in the Kala Gallery as part of What We Hold, New Works by Kala’s 2025-2026 Kala Fellowship artists.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Then get ready for the annual Mini Masterpieces Holiday Gifts Show — equal parts fine art exhibit and most unique holiday shopping experience in Alameda — presented by Art Jam at Rhythmix!

events.description:
San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
San Francisco Bike Party
San Francisco Bike Party (not to be confused with Critical Mass) is a monthly celebration of biking for riders of different ages, types, and skill levels to enjoy. Every month is a different theme and you’re encouraged to dress up.
San Francisco Bike Party is held on the first Friday at 8:00 pm every month (meet at 7:30p, roll at 8p). The starting location and route also changes every month. Check SF Bike Party’s Facebook page for updates.
The rides are fun and safe with stops to dance and socialize along the way. You’ll follow planned routes exploring all different parts of the city each month. They encourage people to bring positivity and contribute to good times while being respectful to others.

Who runs it? Created by a co-op, by and for bike enthusiasts, run by volunteers who plan the routes, test ride them, help participants ride in control, avoid traffic disruption, and not get lost. How SFBP rides: – Stay in the right lane – Stop at red lights – Leave no trace – Ride predictably and in control – Roll past conflict – Ride prepared – When in doubt, “bike party!!”

events.title: SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

events.description: Laurie PielThe Muir Beach Holiday Arts Fair returns to the beautiful Muir Beach Community Center (19 Seacape Drive) on Saturday, December 5 from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Sunday, December 6, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Holiday shoppers can browse charming booths featuring original handmade fine art, crafts, and gourmet holiday treats. With over 50 years of tradition, the Muir Beach Holiday Arts Fair is the perfect reason to take a short 15-minute drive from Highway 101 and escape to the scenic seaside community of Muir Beach for unique holiday gifts. More than 40 local artists from Marin and the Bay Area will showcase their fantastic artwork and colorful crafts, including handmade jewelry, glassware, ceramics, textiles, woodworking, wreaths, ornaments, leather accessories, holiday knick-knacks and gifts from the garden. The beloved Muir Beach Quilters will also be present, offering scarves, gloves, and quilts for sale. The Muir Beach Volunteer Firefighters will sell their popular dog logo clothing, hats, stainless steelware and accessories to help fund their department. Again this year, the Muir Beach Holiday Arts Fair will partner with the California College of the Arts to showcase student artwork. Food and beverages will be available for purchase and a portion of the weekend’s proceeds will help fund community events. For further information, please call (415) 595-7411 or visit our website at muirbeachartsfair.com.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSFPLWe’ll be pausing Laughton’s Southern Gothic thriller, Night of the Hunter, to draw striking frames. We’ll be focusing on the art deco design, dramatic shadows and poses in the film.
Basic materials (pencils, paper, erasers) will be provided. You may bring your own materials, but please no fume-creating paint or paint pens. Watercolor, ink and gouache are fine.

This is a self-led event; there will be no instruction or feedback. However, there will be an opportunity at the end of the session to look at others’ drawings and show your own.
PG, 92 mins., 1955. Closed captions (CC) in English. Due to pauses for drawing, the full film will not be shown.

Discover a wide range of original fine arts and crafts gifts that caters to every taste and budget at 1890 Bryant Studios’ Holiday Market!

Gifts, Jewelry, Stationery, Sculpture, Fine Art, Baked Goods, Ceramics, Wearable Art …and more!
1890 Bryant Studios
Once a mayonnaise factory at the industrial edge of San Francisco’s Mission district, 1890 BryantStreet Studios has become one of the city’s most vibrant and enduring artist hubs. For nearly two decades, the four-story building — where the top three floors house active studios — has welcomed painters, photographers, sculptors, ceramicists, textile artists, jewelers, and others in its creative fold.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

Howard Zinn Book FairIf ever there was a time to create our own history rather than let malevolent people write it for us, that time is now! Meet the people and groups helping build a world that serves everyone at the Howard Zinn Book Fair, Sunday, December 6, from 10am to 6pm, at the San Francisco City College Mission Campus, 1125 Valencia Street. This year’s theme is A Time of Monsters, A Time to Fight.

The Howard Zinn Book Fair started in 2014 as an annual celebration and this year features 40 panel discussions by authors and activists and a big room full of independent presses, community groups, artists, and non-profits. All of our participants focus on empowering people to become engaged in the struggle for a truly participatory and democratic society.

We live in a time when many are asked to survive what can only be called monstrous: authoritarianism, war, state violence, environmental destruction, economic insecurity, forced displacement, attacks on civil rights, and the everyday cruelties of systems built to dehumanize. But throughout history, ordinary people have resisted monstrous situations and individuals in order to take more control of their future.

This year we have dozens of speakers including renowned journalist Dave Zirin, whose new book The People’s Historian: The Outsized Life of Howard Zinn is a groundbreaking profile of our book fair’s namesake, the radical historian and thought leader Howard Zinn.

events.description:
“Free Oakland Up” Market: Shop for Free Treasures (Every Friday-Sunday)
freeoaklandup
Free Oakland UP, a Social Practice Project by Jocelyn Meggait, is open Fridays through Sundays from 12–4 PM, offering free materials for art, collage, and junk journals such as ephemera, electronics parts, books, and household goods. Outdoor items are entirely free to take (just don’t take their tables, bins or shelves), while indoor visitors can choose one free item per person per day, with additional items available for a monetary donation. Some plants and select treasures are for sale. The shop aims to keep usable items out of the landfill.
Original Event Description:
_Free Oakland UP is open Friday to Sunday, 12-4, with new treasures and plants added weekly. Outside: everything is FREE, take as much as you want except my tables, bins and shelves. Loads of materials for collage, assemblage and junk journals: ephemera, typewriter and electronics parts, books, cds and DVDs, magazines, household goods, etc. Inside: ONE free item per person per day and for a fair monetary donation you may choose more. Plants and select treasures are for sale to help pay for rent and expenses. Thank you for keeping treasures out of the landfill._

events.title: 1890 Bryant Street Studios Holiday Market (Dec. 5-6)
events.description:
1890 Bryant

Discover a wide range of original fine arts and crafts gifts that caters to every taste and budget at 1890 Bryant Studios’ Holiday Market!

Gifts, Jewelry, Stationery, Sculpture, Fine Art, Baked Goods, Ceramics, Wearable Art …and more!
1890 Bryant Studios
Once a mayonnaise factory at the industrial edge of San Francisco’s Mission district, 1890 BryantStreet Studios has become one of the city’s most vibrant and enduring artist hubs. For nearly two decades, the four-story building — where the top three floors house active studios — has welcomed painters, photographers, sculptors, ceramicists, textile artists, jewelers, and others in its creative fold.

Find a Treasure! Discover a wide range of original fine arts and crafts gifts that caters to every taste and budget. Don’t miss your chance to visit when the building is open to the public for our Annual Holiday Market, as well as for Spring and Fall Open Studios.
Easy Access! Our location is a breeze to reach via MUNI, and there is free street parking on Florida, and Mariposa streets. Our studios are wheelchair accessible, ensuring a welcoming environment for everyone. Well-behaved kids and furry friends are welcome too!
Entrance to this event is free.
1890 Bryant Street, San Francisco, CA 94110
Saturday + Sunday, Dec 5 + Dec 6, 12PM-5PM

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCuban Rumba Jam: Play, Sing, Dance & Enjoy | Berkeley
La Peña Cultural Center
This free, participatory event has been a staple at La Peña Cultural Center for 12 years due to its incredible fun, and recurs every 1st and 3rd Sunday of each month.
Come enjoy the Afro-Cuban folkloric drums, dances, and songs of rumba. Rumba is the word used for a group of related, community-oriented, music and dance styles in Cuba.
Rumba developed in rural Cuba, with strong influences from African drumming and Spanish poetry and singing.

Come play, sing, dance, or simply watch and enjoy.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

The San Francisco Botanical Garden is one of the most diverse gardens in the world. A unique urban oasis, the garden is a living museum within Golden Gate Park, offering 55 acres of both landscaped gardens and open spaces, and showcasing over 9,000 different kinds of plants from around the world.
One of the most beautiful spots is the Japanese-design inspired “Moon Viewing Garden,” (pictured above) located in the Mild-Temperate Climate section in the Northwest portion of the gardens. [view map]
The garden is always free for San Francisco residents, but visitors can also enjoy this treasure for free on the second Tuesday of every month; plus it’s free on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, and New Year’s Day for everyone.

events.address: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

Opened to the public in 1993, YBCA was founded as the cultural anchor of San Francisco’s Yerba Buena Gardens neighborhood. Centering artists as essential to social and cultural movement, YBCA is reimagining the role an arts institution can play in the community it serves.
YBCA is located in the heart of San Francisco’s SOMA neighborhood, across the street from SFMOMA and the Moscone Convention Center. The main entrance to our galleries and forum event space is at 701 Mission Street. The main entrance to our theater is 700 Howard Street.

events.title: Performance: Kim Shuck’s Poem Celebrates November Dance Shirt
events.venue: San Francisco Public Library, Main Library, Latino Room (lower level)
events.description:
K. ShuckSan Francisco Poet Laureate emerita Kim Shuck, poet Lauren Ito and special guests celebrate Shuck’s new collection November Dance Shirt at SFPL’s Monthly poetry reading.
Kim Shuck was San Francisco’s seventh Poet Laureate. Her poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco. Her most recent book of poetry, November Dance Shirt, was published in 2026, and her book of essays, Noodle, Rant, Tangent, was published in 2022. In her term as Poet Laureate, she hosted scores of free poetry and art workshops for all ages at neighborhood libraries and schools and worked closely with San Francisco Public Library and the San Francisco Arts Commission to launch major citywide initiatives to honor Native American Indigenous Peoples’ heritage.

events.title: Radical Overview About Ditching Technology In-Person
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerNYC LudditesJoin us as the NYC Luddites share how they organized the Summer of Ludd (SoL) in June – July of 2026: 8 days, 150 events, free lunch for 250 people a day, no permits, in a historic heatwave, all organized without social media! SoL included a plurality of events, from radical puppet theater, to teach-ins on Data Center resistance, to jamborees, and workshops for divesting from Big Tech.
Come learn about how they did this and how the Luddite critique can help us make sense of the AI bubble, alienation, and the surveillance state. This movement is historically grounded in the Luddites of the 1810’s who resisted “machines hurtful to commonality, which tear unduly at the social fabric.” As tech billionaires tear at the social fabric around us, Luddites ask, “how can we rebuild it?”

This presentation will include: organizing tactics for reclaiming public space, structures for large-scale projects, digital security + organizing without relying on platforms, tactical playfulness, and base-building for a popular movement against Big Tech.
This event is FREE, PUBLIC, & PARTICIPATORY!
As we like to say in NYC The Event is the Medium!
Summer of Ludd has been covered in publications such as Wired, The Economist, and 404 Media.

events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.title: Hanukkah Klezmer Party with Veretski Pass
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCookie Segelstein
Celebrate Hanukkah with a rollicking klezmer concert at the Jazzschool, presented by legendary Bay Area klezmer trio Veretski Pass. Dust off your dancing shoes and come ready to move to the driving rhythms of traditional Jewish, Ukrainian, and Polish music, as well as original compositions and spirited improvisations in the klezmer tradition. Often raucous, always danceable!
Drawing on centuries-old Eastern European traditions, Veretski Pass offers a unique and exciting combination of virtuosic musicianship and raw energy that has excited audiences internationally for more than two decades. Instrumental in co-creating the “klezmer revival,” a movement which began in the 1970s with the goal of reviving Eastern European Jewish music, the band has performed and recorded hundreds of pieces of Jewish music, drawing on a vast array of sources, including contemporary and 19th-century ethnographic collections.

Performing on original instruments in an unbound, energetic “village style,” Veretski Pass has not only preserved, but reimagined, recomposed, and rearranged Jewish music from Ukraine, Poland, Carpathian-Ruthenia, Bessarabia, and Romania, enhancing and enriching modern klezmer music.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

events.title: Authentic Open-Air German Holiday Market 2026 (Mountain View)
events.description:
GISSVThe German Holiday Market recreates the jovial atmosphere of a traditional open-air, European winter market on Mountain View’s City Hall Plaza. Shop for unique, handcrafted gifts from Germany and local artisans: Wood ornaments and nutcrackers from Germany, Lebkuchen (gingerbread), Stollen, chocolate, toys, ceramics, and knitwear. Taste traditional German sausages and pretzels and warm up with a mug of Glühwein (warm mulled wine), the hallmark of these winter markets. The German Holiday Market offers plenty of activities for the entire family, including live performances and arts and crafts.
The Market is a 10-minute walk from the Mountain View transit center, a lovely stroll along Castro Street where you will find more shopping and more eateries. Just like in Europe, arrive on foot to the Weihnachtsmarkt!
Rain or Shine! Join us! Admission is free!

You are invited to step into Germany for a day, no passport needed. Come enjoy this seasonal celebration!

events.title: Free Beginner Parkour “Urban Ninja” Class
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerFree Beginner Parkour “Urban Ninja” Class
SF Parkour
SF Parkour hosts a free Beginner’s Parkour Class at noon on the second Saturday of each month. It is geared towards first timers and lasts 1.5 hours.
Location: Each month the location rotates through Sunnyvale, UC Berkeley and the Embarcadero in SF. Please check the SF Parkour Facebook page to make sure you have the right date and location before heading out.

The emphasis will be on controlled progression and will cover: philosophy of parkour, training, conditioning and safety tips, and basic movements such as vaults, landings and rolls. Taking photos/videos at this session is discouraged. Attendees are also welcome to hang out, continue training, or have an open jam after the class ends.
Additional Info:

The scheduled dates and times will be adhered to unless otherwise specified due to holidays, conflicting events, special events, visiting guests, etc. This way attendees can plan well ahead of time.
All ages, sexes, and experience levels are welcome. Ages 18 and under must have parental permission.
Beginners are always welcome and can get help at any of the sessions.
Each of the sessions will include warm ups, help for beginners, conditioning and training, open jamming, cool downs, and clean-up time.
Wear comfortable clothing you can move freely in, a good pair of running shoes, and bring along some water.

Come join a volunteer work party at The School Farm every second Saturday from noon to 4 pm to lend a hand and learn about farm work.

The School Farm is located on the campus of the Academy of Arts and Sciences and the School of the Arts – 555 Portola Dr. San Francisco. Enter gate on O’shaughnessy Blvd just before it crosses Portola. It’s close to 36, 44, 48, and 52 Muni lines. From the parking area at the top, proceed on foot to the right, down the hill towards the athletic field. Limited parking is available further down the driveway at the loading dock, but please do not park on the grass. The farm is behind the east bleachers across the field.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

San Francisco, CA — Winston Smith’s Studio Fallout and legendary punk record label Alternative Tentacles are teaming up once again to present The 4th Annual Bat Show: Nocturnal Emissions & Holiday Havoc!, a celebration of punk art, creative mischief, and one of underground culture’s most recognizable icons.

Winston Smith has been closely associated with Jello Biafra and Alternative Tentacles since the label’s early days, creating artwork for its records, posters, and promotional materials. This year’s exhibition brings together artists from near and far, each offering their own interpretation of Winston’s original bat. events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

Pi.1415926535
The free PresidiGo Shuttle system welcomes park visitors, residents, and employees with fully accessible shuttles and bike racks.
There are two PresidiGo Shuttle services, each with different policies and guidelines – Around the Park and Downtown.

Downtown (Free on Weekends)
The Downtown express route make stops at the Presidio Transit Center on the Main Post, the Letterman District, Union Street/Van Ness Avenue, Embarcadero BART, and the Transbay Terminal.
The shuttle operates from 5:45 am to 9:30 pm on weekdays and 10 am to 7:30 pm on weekends. On weekdays, during the evening commute (leaving the Presidio only) from 4-7:40 pm, a valid MUNI Passport (not a MUNI Fast Pass) is required. No pass is required on weekends.
It’s free for Presidio Employees and Residents every day with an appropriate boarding pass. Connecting service to Caltrain is available.
The Downtown PresidiGo does not operate on federal holidays.
Around the Park (Every Day – 2 Routes)
Around the Park is free and available to visitors, residents, and employees all day. The shuttle runs two continuous 30-minute loops:

The Crissy Field Route serves the northern Presidio including the Main Post, Golden Gate Bridge, Fort Scott and Letterman District

events.title: SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

The Cow Palace, 2600 Geneva Avenue, Daly City, CA
Saturdays and Sundays, November 21 to December 20, 2026, plus Friday, November 27, the day after Thanksgiving, from 10 am to 6 pm
