events.title: Adam Shulman Trio Plays a Charlie Brown Christmas
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerAdam ShulmanJoin pianist Adam Shulman and his trio at the Jazzschool for a cozy holiday tribute to Bay Area jazz legend Vince Guaraldi and his iconic soundtrack to Charles Schulz’s 1965 TV special, A Charlie Brown Christmas. This event features two showtimes: an earlier family concert with a shortened runtime from 5:30-7pm, and a regular concert at 8pm.
Among the most beloved holiday albums of all time, A Charlie Brown Christmas has been certified Triple Platinum, was voted into the GRAMMY Hall of Fame in 2007, and was added to the Library of Congress’ National Recording Registry’s list of “culturally, historically, or aesthetically important” American recordings.

The album features a series of Christmas standards, including the Guaraldi originals “Christmas Time Is Here” and “Skating,” classic holiday songs like “O Tannenbaum” and “What Child Is This,” and the quintessential Peanuts Christmas tune, “Linus and Lucy.”
Pianist, composer, and arranger Adam Shulman has been a staple of the San Francisco jazz scene since he moved to the city in 2002. As a music student at UC Santa Cruz, Shulman studied jazz piano with the late, beloved piano master Smith Dobson, going on to work with internationally renowned artists such as Stefon Harris, Miguel Zenón, Luciana Souza, Paula West, Larry Coryell, Bobby Hutcherson, and the Glenn Miller Orchestra.

events.title: San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride (Every Third Saturday)
events.description:
San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride (Every Third Saturday)
Midnight Mystery Ride
Every third Saturday, you are invited to bicycle with the San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride as they set out to a new mystery location in SF.
Where to meet? They’ll post ride start locations on their website and Facebook page, the day of the ride only; there’s no advance warning. The ride happens every third Saturday.
Participants are expected to:

Meet at a local bar before midnight on Saturday
Depart for a ride at midnight
Bring provisions for sharing at ride destination
Be awesome.

Ride start locations will be posted to their website the day of the ride. Only the ride leader knows where they’re going, so bring your sense of adventure. Rides are strictly NRLB (No Rider Left Behind) and generally around 5 miles – all levels of cyclist are welcome. They ride rain or shine.

freeoaklandup
Free Oakland UP, a Social Practice Project by Jocelyn Meggait, is open Fridays through Sundays from 12–4 PM, offering free materials for art, collage, and junk journals such as ephemera, electronics parts, books, and household goods. Outdoor items are entirely free to take (just don’t take their tables, bins or shelves), while indoor visitors can choose one free item per person per day, with additional items available for a monetary donation. Some plants and select treasures are for sale. The shop aims to keep usable items out of the landfill.

Plants and select treasures are for sale to help pay for rent and expenses. Thank you for keeping treasures out of the landfill._

events.description:
Museum of the Game
​Can love be measured? For over a hundred years, we have been on a quest to measure love and uncover the principles of romantic affection. . .

​This month, we’re reading “Love Tester Machines,” a history of devices that promised to predict whether two people were a match. To see how they worked firsthand, we’re taking Gray Area book club offsite for the first time, to the Musée Mécanique, the largest museum of arcades in the US.

Bring your friend, partner, or check your compatibility with another book club regular! At the end of the day, it’s just a gamble . . .or not?

SF’s 2026 Union Square’s Great Holiday Tree (Nov. 27 – Jan. 1)
Macy's
For generations, Union Square’s iconic Christmas tree has been a centerpiece of San Francisco’s holiday season, drawing visitors downtown to see the city sparkle for the holidays. But 2026 brings a big change to this beloved tradition: after years of towering artificial trees, Union Square is welcoming a real, 60-foot white fir for the first time since 2010.
2026 update: The live tree arrived in Union Square on November 19 and is scheduled to be lit on Friday, November 27, 2026 (the day after Thanksgiving).
The tree was grown in Burney, in Shasta County, and traveled to San Francisco to become the centerpiece of the city’s holiday celebrations. It’s a major change from the previous Macy’s-sponsored artificial tree, which stood more than 83 feet tall and featured 43,000 LED lights and 700 ornaments.

Macy’s is no longer sponsoring the tree, but the holiday tradition lives on. The Union Square Alliance and the city are stepping in to keep a festive centerpiece in the plaza, with the tree lighting up the square throughout the holiday season.
Stop by Union Square Plaza to see San Francisco’s newest Christmas tree, just across the street from the Macy’s flagship store. The tree is scheduled to remain illuminated through January 1, 2027.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.address: Geary and Powell, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
SF’s 2026 Union Square’s Great Holiday Tree (Nov. 27 – Jan. 1)
Macy's
For generations, Union Square’s iconic Christmas tree has been a centerpiece of San Francisco’s holiday season, drawing visitors downtown to see the city sparkle for the holidays. But 2026 brings a big change to this beloved tradition: after years of towering artificial trees, Union Square is welcoming a real, 60-foot white fir for the first time since 2010.
2026 update: The live tree arrived in Union Square on November 19 and is scheduled to be lit on Friday, November 27, 2026 (the day after Thanksgiving).
The tree was grown in Burney, in Shasta County, and traveled to San Francisco to become the centerpiece of the city’s holiday celebrations. It’s a major change from the previous Macy’s-sponsored artificial tree, which stood more than 83 feet tall and featured 43,000 LED lights and 700 ornaments.

Macy’s is no longer sponsoring the tree, but the holiday tradition lives on. The Union Square Alliance and the city are stepping in to keep a festive centerpiece in the plaza, with the tree lighting up the square throughout the holiday season.
Stop by Union Square Plaza to see San Francisco’s newest Christmas tree, just across the street from the Macy’s flagship store. The tree is scheduled to remain illuminated through January 1, 2027.

Lindy in the Park

On the very rare occasion when they cancel, they’ll make a new posting on their website, usually by 10am on Sunday. Lindy in the Park’s Schedule FAQ

No partner is required, as they rotate leaders and followers throughout the lesson.

events.address: Geary and Powell, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
SF’s 2026 Union Square’s Great Holiday Tree (Nov. 27 – Jan. 1)
Macy's
For generations, Union Square’s iconic Christmas tree has been a centerpiece of San Francisco’s holiday season, drawing visitors downtown to see the city sparkle for the holidays. But 2026 brings a big change to this beloved tradition: after years of towering artificial trees, Union Square is welcoming a real, 60-foot white fir for the first time since 2010.
2026 update: The live tree arrived in Union Square on November 19 and is scheduled to be lit on Friday, November 27, 2026 (the day after Thanksgiving).
The tree was grown in Burney, in Shasta County, and traveled to San Francisco to become the centerpiece of the city’s holiday celebrations. It’s a major change from the previous Macy’s-sponsored artificial tree, which stood more than 83 feet tall and featured 43,000 LED lights and 700 ornaments.

Macy’s is no longer sponsoring the tree, but the holiday tradition lives on. The Union Square Alliance and the city are stepping in to keep a festive centerpiece in the plaza, with the tree lighting up the square throughout the holiday season.
Stop by Union Square Plaza to see San Francisco’s newest Christmas tree, just across the street from the Macy’s flagship store. The tree is scheduled to remain illuminated through January 1, 2027.

events.description:
San Francisco Botanical Garden’s Free Day (2nd Tuesdays)
Saxon Holt / SF Botanical Gardens
The San Francisco Botanical Garden is one of the most diverse gardens in the world. A unique urban oasis, the garden is a living museum within Golden Gate Park, offering 55 acres of both landscaped gardens and open spaces, and showcasing over 9,000 different kinds of plants from around the world.
One of the most beautiful spots is the Japanese-design inspired “Moon Viewing Garden,” (pictured above) located in the Mild-Temperate Climate section in the Northwest portion of the gardens. [view map]
The garden is always free for San Francisco residents, but visitors can also enjoy this treasure for free on the second Tuesday of every month; plus it’s free on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, and New Year’s Day for everyone.

Early bird? Come by any day and get in for free from 7:30-9 am.
San Francisco Botanical Garden Free Days

Second Tuesday of every month
Thanksgiving, Christmas & New Year’s Day

SF’s 2026 Union Square’s Great Holiday Tree (Nov. 27 – Jan. 1)
Macy's
For generations, Union Square’s iconic Christmas tree has been a centerpiece of San Francisco’s holiday season, drawing visitors downtown to see the city sparkle for the holidays. But 2026 brings a big change to this beloved tradition: after years of towering artificial trees, Union Square is welcoming a real, 60-foot white fir for the first time since 2010.
2026 update: The live tree arrived in Union Square on November 19 and is scheduled to be lit on Friday, November 27, 2026 (the day after Thanksgiving).
The tree was grown in Burney, in Shasta County, and traveled to San Francisco to become the centerpiece of the city’s holiday celebrations. It’s a major change from the previous Macy’s-sponsored artificial tree, which stood more than 83 feet tall and featured 43,000 LED lights and 700 ornaments.

Macy’s is no longer sponsoring the tree, but the holiday tradition lives on. The Union Square Alliance and the city are stepping in to keep a festive centerpiece in the plaza, with the tree lighting up the square throughout the holiday season.
Stop by Union Square Plaza to see San Francisco’s newest Christmas tree, just across the street from the Macy’s flagship store. The tree is scheduled to remain illuminated through January 1, 2027.

San Francisco Bike Party
San Francisco Bike Party (not to be confused with Critical Mass) is a monthly celebration of biking for riders of different ages, types, and skill levels to enjoy. Every month is a different theme and you’re encouraged to dress up.
San Francisco Bike Party is held on the first Friday at 8:00 pm every month (meet at 7:30p, roll at 8p). The starting location and route also changes every month. Check SF Bike Party’s Facebook page for updates.
The rides are fun and safe with stops to dance and socialize along the way. You’ll follow planned routes exploring all different parts of the city each month. They encourage people to bring positivity and contribute to good times while being respectful to others.

Who runs it? Created by a co-op, by and for bike enthusiasts, run by volunteers who plan the routes, test ride them, help participants ride in control, avoid traffic disruption, and not get lost. How SFBP rides: – Stay in the right lane – Stop at red lights – Leave no trace – Ride predictably and in control – Roll past conflict – Ride prepared – When in doubt, “bike party!!”

events.title: Free Beginner Parkour “Urban Ninja” Class
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerFree Beginner Parkour “Urban Ninja” Class
SF Parkour
SF Parkour hosts a free Beginner’s Parkour Class at noon on the second Saturday of each month. It is geared towards first timers and lasts 1.5 hours.
Location: Each month the location rotates through Sunnyvale, UC Berkeley and the Embarcadero in SF. Please check the SF Parkour Facebook page to make sure you have the right date and location before heading out.

The emphasis will be on controlled progression and will cover: philosophy of parkour, training, conditioning and safety tips, and basic movements such as vaults, landings and rolls. Taking photos/videos at this session is discouraged. Attendees are also welcome to hang out, continue training, or have an open jam after the class ends.
Additional Info:

The scheduled dates and times will be adhered to unless otherwise specified due to holidays, conflicting events, special events, visiting guests, etc. This way attendees can plan well ahead of time.
All ages, sexes, and experience levels are welcome. Ages 18 and under must have parental permission.
Beginners are always welcome and can get help at any of the sessions.
Each of the sessions will include warm ups, help for beginners, conditioning and training, open jamming, cool downs, and clean-up time.
Wear comfortable clothing you can move freely in, a good pair of running shoes, and bring along some water.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerEco SF School Farm Volunteer Work Day | SF
National Park Service
Come join a volunteer work party at The School Farm every second Saturday from noon to 4 pm to lend a hand and learn about farm work.
All skill levels and abilities are welcome, even for moral support and comic relief. They will provide some water and maybe a snack, and plenty of well worn gloves, but If you’d like, bring some more refreshments to share or your favorite personal protective equipment. For more info, contact sam@eco-sf.org.

The School Farm is located on the campus of the Academy of Arts and Sciences and the School of the Arts – 555 Portola Dr. San Francisco. Enter gate on O’shaughnessy Blvd just before it crosses Portola. It’s close to 36, 44, 48, and 52 Muni lines. From the parking area at the top, proceed on foot to the right, down the hill towards the athletic field. Limited parking is available further down the driveway at the loading dock, but please do not park on the grass. The farm is behind the east bleachers across the field.

events.description:

Every second Saturday of the month, EXIT Theatre invites writers, actors, directors, theater creators and theater audiences alike to a free evening of quick script-making and flash-fried performance.

9 pm: Writing sprint where writers have 30 minutes to generate original monologues based around that night’s pre-generated prompts

events.description:
San Francisco Botanical Garden’s Free Day (2nd Tuesdays)
Saxon Holt / SF Botanical Gardens
The San Francisco Botanical Garden is one of the most diverse gardens in the world. A unique urban oasis, the garden is a living museum within Golden Gate Park, offering 55 acres of both landscaped gardens and open spaces, and showcasing over 9,000 different kinds of plants from around the world.
One of the most beautiful spots is the Japanese-design inspired “Moon Viewing Garden,” (pictured above) located in the Mild-Temperate Climate section in the Northwest portion of the gardens. [view map]
The garden is always free for San Francisco residents, but visitors can also enjoy this treasure for free on the second Tuesday of every month; plus it’s free on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, and New Year’s Day for everyone.

Early bird? Come by any day and get in for free from 7:30-9 am.

events.address: Park Blvd. and Lincoln Blvd., San Franciso, CA
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerFree PresidiGo Shuttle | Downtown to Presidio
Pi.1415926535
The free PresidiGo Shuttle system welcomes park visitors, residents, and employees with fully accessible shuttles and bike racks.
There are two PresidiGo Shuttle services, each with different policies and guidelines – Around the Park and Downtown.

Downtown (Free on Weekends)
The Downtown express route make stops at the Presidio Transit Center on the Main Post, the Letterman District, Union Street/Van Ness Avenue, Embarcadero BART, and the Transbay Terminal.
The shuttle operates from 5:45 am to 9:30 pm on weekdays and 10 am to 7:30 pm on weekends. On weekdays, during the evening commute (leaving the Presidio only) from 4-7:40 pm, a valid MUNI Passport (not a MUNI Fast Pass) is required. No pass is required on weekends.
It’s free for Presidio Employees and Residents every day with an appropriate boarding pass. Connecting service to Caltrain is available.
The Downtown PresidiGo does not operate on federal holidays.
Around the Park (Every Day – 2 Routes)
Around the Park is free and available to visitors, residents, and employees all day. The shuttle runs two continuous 30-minute loops:

The Crissy Field Route serves the northern Presidio including the Main Post, Golden Gate Bridge, Fort Scott and Letterman District
The Presidio Hills Route is a bi-directional route serving the Letterman District, Main Post, Inspiration Point, Washington Boulevard, Baker Beach, and Public Health Service Di...

events.title: San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride (Every Third Saturday)
events.description:
San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride (Every Third Saturday)
Midnight Mystery Ride
Every third Saturday, you are invited to bicycle with the San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride as they set out to a new mystery location in SF.
Where to meet? They’ll post ride start locations on their website and Facebook page, the day of the ride only; there’s no advance warning. The ride happens every third Saturday.
Participants are expected to:

Meet at a local bar before midnight on Saturday
Depart for a ride at midnight
Bring provisions for sharing at ride destination
Be awesome.

Ride start locations will be posted to their website the day of the ride. Only the ride leader knows where they’re going, so bring your sense of adventure. Rides are strictly NRLB (No Rider Left Behind) and generally around 5 miles – all levels of cyclist are welcome. They ride rain or shine.

events.title: San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
events.description:
San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
San Francisco Bike Party
San Francisco Bike Party (not to be confused with Critical Mass) is a monthly celebration of biking for riders of different ages, types, and skill levels to enjoy. Every month is a different theme and you’re encouraged to dress up.
San Francisco Bike Party is held on the first Friday at 8:00 pm every month (meet at 7:30p, roll at 8p). The starting location and route also changes every month. Check SF Bike Party’s Facebook page for updates.
The rides are fun and safe with stops to dance and socialize along the way. You’ll follow planned routes exploring all different parts of the city each month. They encourage people to bring positivity and contribute to good times while being respectful to others.

Who runs it? Created by a co-op, by and for bike enthusiasts, run by volunteers who plan the routes, test ride them, help participants ride in control, avoid traffic disruption, and not get lost. How SFBP rides: – Stay in the right lane – Stop at red lights – Leave no trace – Ride predictably and in control – Roll past conflict – Ride prepared – When in doubt, “bike party!!”

Wear comfortable clothing you can move freely in, a good pair of running shoes, and bring along some water.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerFree PresidiGo Shuttle | Downtown to Presidio
Pi.1415926535
The free PresidiGo Shuttle system welcomes park visitors, residents, and employees with fully accessible shuttles and bike racks.
There are two PresidiGo Shuttle services, each with different policies and guidelines – Around the Park and Downtown.

Downtown (Free on Weekends)
The Downtown express route make stops at the Presidio Transit Center on the Main Post, the Letterman District, Union Street/Van Ness Avenue, Embarcadero BART, and the Transbay Terminal.
The shuttle operates from 5:45 am to 9:30 pm on weekdays and 10 am to 7:30 pm on weekends. On weekdays, during the evening commute (leaving the Presidio only) from 4-7:40 pm, a valid MUNI Passport (not a MUNI Fast Pass) is required. No pass is required on weekends.
It’s free for Presidio Employees and Residents every day with an appropriate boarding pass. Connecting service to Caltrain is available.
The Downtown PresidiGo does not operate on federal holidays.
Around the Park (Every Day – 2 Routes)
Around the Park is free and available to visitors, residents, and employees all day. The shuttle runs two continuous 30-minute loops:

The Crissy Field Route serves the northern Presidio including the Main Post, Golden Gate Bridge, Fort Scott and Letterman District

The San Francisco History Association hosts monthly talks which explore our city’s enchanting history in depth.
Each month, a local history expert hosts a themed talk usually accompanied by a slide show with light refreshments.

Monthly presentations cover a dizzyingly diverse variety of SF history aspects, from the history of the San Francisco Fire Department to appreciation of our unique Victorian houses to vintage stories and photos from Playland-at-the-Beach.
San Francisco History Association Meeting
The last Tuesday of every month (except December)
– Doors open at 7 pm; program begins about 7:45 pm
– Newman Hall, Congregation Sherith Israel, 2266 California (at Webster), SF 94115.
– $10 General Public; FREE if you’re an SFHA Member

events.title: Whiskey in the Park 2027: Taste 100+ Whiskies (San Jose)
events.venue: History Park @ Kelly Park San Jose
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerWhisky EduStep into a whiskey lover’s paradise at the 7th Annual Whiskey in the Park at History Park San Jose on Saturday, June 19, 2027.
Spend the evening exploring more than 100 whiskies from around the world while enjoying the outdoor setting of History Park, live music, food, and whiskey education.
Guests can meet distillers, discover the stories behind different whiskies, compare flavors, and enjoy pours representing regions including Scotland, Ireland, Japan, Texas, and beyond.
General Admission includes the full whiskey tasting experience, savory food, live music, and a souvenir tasting glass. Additional experiences include the Whiskey Bottle Pull, an optional premium masterclass, and VIP/afterparty upgrades.
Whether you’re a longtime whiskey enthusiast or simply curious to learn more, Whiskey in the Park brings together whiskey, food, music, education, and community for an evening in San Jose.
Date: Saturday, June 19, 2027
Time: 5:00 PM–10:00 PM
Location: History Park @ Kelly Park, 635 Phelan Avenue, San Jose, CA 95112

events.title: San Francisco Opera End of Year Public Market
events.description:
Happening Sunday, November 29, the San Francisco Opera End of Year Public Market in partnership with the Artyhood Foundation is taking place in Memorial Court, adjacent to the War Memorial.
They’re bringing together local artisans, talented artists, and delicious food vendors for a free, vibrant community event celebrating San Francisco Opera’s season.
Stop by to grab a bite to eat and discover unique handmade wares from local creators.
📍 Memorial Court, San Francisco
🗓️ Sunday, November 29 | 11:30 AM – 4:00 PM
🎟️ Free and open to all!

events.title: Civic Center Plaza Tree Lighting 2026
events.description:
Join us for a festive evening at Civic Center Plaza as we illuminate the holiday season! The annual Civic Center Plaza Tree Lighting event returns December 2, 4-7pm! Add this fun, free, family-friendly event to your holiday calendar; featuring festive performances, with the night’s lineup including music, performances, and appearances from The Tap Dancing Christmas Trees, the San Francisco Boys Chorus, the Festivus Band, the Grinch and the man-of-the-hour: Santa! With the night of performances all led by the Master of Ceremonies: award-winning performer Rotimi Agbabiaka!
RSVP for an event day reminder on Eventbrite.
The event also features “snow” flurries, where kids (and kids at heart) can twirl and dance through the falling snow, while in the Makers Village, the San Francisco Public Library will host a book giveaway and SF Etsy will lead holiday-themed activities: play snow, holiday crowns, ornament painting, letter writing to Santa, and coloring station! Bites will be available for purchase, along with a full bar featuring seasonal favorites.
The event takes place across from an illuminated City Hall in Civic Center Plaza. Event begins promptly at 4pm, with the lighting of Civic Center’s 50-foot noble fir at 5:30pm. Happening rain or shine!
Those who are not walking to the event are encouraged to take BART/Muni or park in the Civic Center Garage.
